#1752. Serie A preview: AC Milan vs. Frosinone – Team news, opposition insight, stats and prediction

Milan will return to action on Sunday evening, hoping to pick up where they left off before the international break with a strong performance against Frosinone.

If we look at the league, it has been a very decent start to the season for Ruben Amorim and his men. However, they are yet to win three games on the trot, so tomorrow’s encounter is a fantastic chance for them to really show their worth.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It won’t be easy, though. Amorim said during his press conference that it’s hard to identify the movement patterns of Frosinone, who certainly have the ability to make life difficult for the Rossoneri.

Game date: Sunday, November 22 Kick-off time: 18:00 (CET) Venue: San Siro Referee: Luca Pairetto (VAR: Pezzuto)

Some good news arrived on Saturday morning as Strahinja Pavlovic was deemed fit enough to be called up for the game. It’s not certain whether he will start or not, but Amorim at least said that he’s happy to have the Serbian and ‘his fire’ back.

A few days ago, it was also confirmed that Mike Maignan will be at the manager’s disposal despite the injury scare with France. Of course, it’s not all perfect on the injury front as Matteo Gabbia, Fikayo Tomori, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Alexis Saelemaekers and Samuel Chukwueze are still sidelined.

Anyway, moving on to the predicted starting eleven, it was initially thought that Amorim would field the same one as we saw against Genoa. However, he made it very clear during the presser that Musah won’t play as a left-back, so there will indeed be some changes.

According to the latest reports, the American will still start but in midfield instead, allowing Adrien Rabiot to have a slightly more advanced role. It also means that Davide Bartesaghi will come into the eleven, currently ahead of Pervis Estupinan in the race.

Alphadjo Cisse has been in red-hot form lately but it seems Amorim wants to manage expectations a little, with the youngster tipped to start on the bench. Christian Pulisic should thus have a role on the flank as opposed to in the centre, although one would imagine everything will be a bit fluid.

It’s no surprise to see that Goncalo Ramos should start up front, but of course, he will need to get going with the goalscoring sooner rather than later. Francesco Camarda is knocking on the door, as is Cisse who has been tested in that role before.

Predicted Milan XI (4-3-3): Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Diawara, Bartesaghi; Musah, Modric, Rabiot; Moreira, Ramos, Pulisic.

Predicted bench: Torriani, P. Terracciano, F. Terracciano, Pavlovic, Vladimirov, Estupinan, Jashari, Comotto, Hutchinson, Cisse, Camarda.

Injuries & suspensions: Gabbia, Tomori, Loftus-Cheek, Saelemaekers and Chukwueze.

Frosinone have definitely been one of the surprises of the season so far. After a very strong Serie B campaign with 81 points and only three games lost, they secured direct promotion to the top tier (finishing second) and have been making the most of the adventure.

They are currently on 20 points after eleven games, winning six, drawing two and losing three, which has put them in sixth place. That’s very strong for a newcomer and for a coach who is only in his second season with the club, especially considering the upset against Como.

It’s the 56-year-old’s second attempt at Serie A after coaching Cremonese for half a season in 2022-23. He didn’t manage a single win then, so you can definitely say that the performance so far has been great revenge for him.

So, what is behind this rise? As pointed out by Gazzetta dello Sport, the direct style of play has been key for Frosinone. As opposed to Milan, who want to see a lot of the ball, they are willing to have less possession and break on the counter.

It doesn’t mean that they sit back, though. In fact, it has been the opposite as they are the highest-pressing team in the league. The strategy thus seems to be to force mistakes out of the opponents, while also making sure that they are direct in possession.

While collective effort deserves most of the praise, it has definitely helped that the likes of Giacomo Calo, Giorgi Kvernadze and Antonio Raimondo – among others – have performed at a very high level. They aren’t exactly big-name players, so a lot of them are having their breakout seasons.

Moving on to actual team news, the situation up front is not ideal for Frosinone as their top scorer, the aforementioned Antonio Raimondo, is out injured. Birigilea, who is on two goals, is set to replace him in the No.9 position.

The Milan academy product Sebastiano Desplanches, who left the club four years ago, will be on the bench. He’s yet to make an appearance this season, with Alvini preferring Lorenzo Palmisani instead.

Predicted Frosinone XI (4-2-3-1): Palmisani; Oyono, Calvani, Monterisi, Terzic; Calo, Masini; Ghedjemis; Schmid, Kvernadze; Birigilea.

Predicted bench: Desplanches, Pisseri, Cittadini, Tchato, Amey, Akpoguma, Fayed, El Azzouzi, Cichella, Hasa, Fini, Zerbin, Bobcek.

Injuries & suspensions: Bracaglia, Grillitsch and Raimondo.

This fixture has only been played six times, but even with such a small sample size, it’s clear that Milan are the favourites with four wins and two draws so far. They have won the last three as well, spread across the 2023-24 and 2018-19 seasons.

That said, the most recent encounter was a dramatic one, if you like. Olivier Giroud opened the scoring for Milan away from home but then Frosinone scored twice. Thanks to goals from Matteo Gabbia and Luka Jovic, the Rossoneri were able to turn it back in their favour.

The last time at San Siro, meanwhile, it was a great 3-1 win as Jovic, Pulisic and Tomori found the back of the net. Most of you will remember the American’s goal, as it was Maignan who assisted him with a fantastic pass.

➤ Milan are unbeaten in all six previous meetings against Frosinone in Serie A (W4 D2): among the teams against which they have never lost in the competition, the Rossoneri have played more games only against Pisa (14 – six also against Crotone and Lecco).

➤ Milan have scored at least three goals in four of their six Serie A matches against Frosinone, producing 15 goals overall, an average of 2.5 per game. Only against Pescara (2.9) have they recorded a higher average, among the opponents they have faced on at least five occasions (2.5 also against Casale and Messina).

➤ Frosinone have won six games this season, drawing two and losing three. Only three newly promoted teams in the last 40 years have recorded more wins in their first 12 Serie A games of the season: Bari in 1994/95 (seven), Chievo in 2001/02 (seven), and Hellas Verona in 2013/14 (seven).

➤ Milan have won four of their last five league games (L1), scoring at least two goals in each, after failing to win three of their previous four (D3). The last time they scored more than one goal in consecutive Serie A matches was between September 2020 and January 2021, when they managed 15 games.

➤ Although Frosinone are unbeaten in three of their five away games this season (W1 D2), they have won just two of their last 27 away games in Serie A (including previous participations), with 10 draws and 15 defeats.

➤ Milan have failed to win four of their last seven Serie A games played after the international break (D2 L2). On the other hand, Frosinone are unbeaten in three of their last five top-flight matches immediately following Italy matches (W2 D1).

➤ Frosinone have attempted the most counterattacks from advantageous situations in Serie A this season: 22, almost double the number of any other team. On the other hand, Milan are the only team that haven’t allowed a single counterattack when trailing in the current campaign.

➤ Only Juventus (79) have attempted more long-range shots than Frosinone (77) this season. On the other hand, Milan are the team that have attempted the fewest shots from outside the area (30) and the one that have conceded the most shots from outside the area in relation to the total conceded, 44%.

➤ Adrien Rabiot has earned the most points for his team from direct goal contributions this season, having scored 10 goals and assisted four times. In the most recent matchday, he became the first Milan midfielder to be involved in at least one goal in six consecutive league appearances since Kaká in 2004 (who managed seven).

➤ Only Matías Soulé (80) has been involved in more sequences ending with a shot than Giacomo Calò (76) in this Serie A. The Frosinone player has scored five goals in the current campaign and only one midfielder has scored more goals in the first 12 matchdays in the top flight for a newly promoted team in the three points for a win era: Hidetoshi Nakata with Perugia in 1998/99 (six).

Since Frosinone like to play on the counterattacks, one player who I think could be crucial for Milan is Musah. As he’s set to start in midfield and not at left-back, the feeling is that his main role will be to prevent the opponents from having too much open space on the counter.

Further up the pitch, I’m excited to see Moreira. He got himself a goal in Belgium’s win over Italy and he has looked a lot better on the right flank ever since the derby performance. He can definitely make the difference with his skill.

As for Frosinone, it’s obvious that Calo is the man whom Milan will want to stop. He likes to dictate the play and if he’s allowed too much time on the ball, identifying his teammates in good positions, then there could be trouble for the Rossoneri.

It will also be interesting to see if Birigilea can fill the shoes of Raimondo. He bagged a brace against Lecce but in the last two games, he failed to find the back of the net. He will surely be keen to get back on target.

A lot of people are expecting this to be a high-scoring affair and that’s a very reasonable take, given how both teams play. That said, I think this could be one where Milan actually get their defence in order and don’t concede, even if that might be a somewhat optimistic prediction.

#1751. Arsenal teach Chelsea a lesson in how to be champions

This is how champions are supposed to play and, although the Arsenal home support have not seen a team defend their place at the apex of English league football for two decades, they knew it when they saw it.

The chase was on for Mikel Arteta’s team within two minutes when Morgan Rogers, the man who might have moved to Arsenal this summer, put his new club Chelsea in the lead. So unfolded a thrilling 100 minutes of Premier League competition. Arsenal were the better team in terms of ambition and attack even if one could not discount Chelsea until the very last moment.

Others might have crumbled. That Chelsea did not will give Xabi Alonso hope for a team that did not feature the injured Moisés Caicedo and is now without the departed Enzo Fernández. Yet he will also recognise that his childhood friend from San Sebastián in the other dugout has created a side that treated the game, and their place in it, with an urgency that looks different. The first two minutes might have been ragged for Arsenal but after that they did not let the game happen to them.

Morgan Rogers fires Chelsea in front inside TWO minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/ca8cqnT2Wm

Instead, Arteta’s players drove this contest, and the sequence of chances that came and went was dizzying at times. Their best players scored the two goals. First Kai Havertz, who now has three in four games this season, and then the captain Martin Ødegaard who dispatched what would be the winner.

"A spear through the heart of Chelsea!" Martin Odegaard puts Arsenal in front at the Emirates 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5deEQykjck

Ødegaard looked like the veteran of a title-winning season, and a deep run in the World Cup – an accomplished, shrewd performer in a midfield that was fought over ferociously all afternoon.

As for the game’s defining moment – it would be hard to overlook the feint from Havertz for the winning goal. It deceived the Chelsea players around him and created the channel for Christos Tzolis’s cross to reach Ødegaard. His goal was a close copy, in style and personnel, of the one he scored against Manchester City in the Community Shield but it was crowned by Havertz’s bluff. He shaped to take the ball and let it run under his foot at the last moment.

This was Chelsea’s first defeat in three – leaving only Arsenal and City with nine points from their first three games – although the seven goals conceded is the standout. For all the jet fuel in their attack they keep conceding. This was a much more exacting test than Fulham and Brighton previously, but even so. Alonso has introduced his preferred back three, often a back five, and it is a work in progress.

Arsenal have set the standard in that regard and they were uncompromising again. They did not replicate the errors that led to the Rogers goal and they pushed the limits at all times. Gabriel Magalhães kicked Emi Martínez in the head competing for a ball in the Chelsea area. Myles Lewis-Skelly went after João Pedro. Ben White and Roméo Lavia saw things differently in the first half. This Arsenal team does not shy away from those confrontations in the way their predecessors often did.

In fact, it was notable just how furiously Rogers reacted to Declan Rice when the two England team-mates converged as the Chelsea man charged off to join a late counter-attack. The bad feeling lingered even after the game when Rogers seemed unwilling to forgive. Rice had applied the minimum contact and the maximum cynicism to stop Rogers while the attention of referee Chris Kavanagh was elsewhere.

"He's FUMING Morgan Rogers!" 😳 pic.twitter.com/FciivEedvh

All that ringcraft was one thing, but it should be said that Arsenal were excellent in setting an attacking tempo that will be hell for any team to live with – especially at the Emirates. Havertz is now Arteta’s centre-forward of choice in the absence of a big summer acquisition. Viktor Gyökeres made a late substitute’s appearance – his first minutes of the season. The hierarchy is clear: last season’s great goalscoring hope is now back-up.

“Exceptional” was how Arteta described his team’s response to the early Rogers goal. They had twice failed to clear the ball in their own area when first Maxence Lacroix and then Jorrel Hato created the chance. Rogers’s right foot half-volley was not struck on the full, but it was placed perfectly inside the post with the necessary bounce and skip to mean David Raya never got behind it.

Arteta’s squad runs deep enough that in the closing stages he could relieve his midfield with two Spanish World Cup-winning substitutes – Martín Zubimendi and Mikel Merino. Then there was Noni Madueke on for Bukayo Saka, understudy and first-choice for club and country. This was not Saka’s day in the way it has been in the past, although a very promising shot of his was stopped by Martinez in the first half.

In the pounding that Chelsea took after they went into the lead, Riccardo Calafiori had an equaliser within minutes that was disallowed by VAR on an offside call. The left-back was the third in sequence to try to force the ball over the line from a Rice free-kick. Calafiori was successful, but the second of his team-mates to try, Ezri Konsa, had been offside when he connected.

For the equaliser it was Havertz, accelerating cautiously at first and then full-on with his left foot from the right-side. Ødegaard was well-placed to prevent Lacroix getting close but in truth the challenge never had the force required. Havertz’s shot was not totally convincing but then neither was Martinez’s attempt to save it – every bit as uncertain as Raya for the Chelsea goal.

A precise finish from Kai Havertz and Arsenal are level! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DqL1MEX4zN

Chelsea had profited from the quick ball out to their right where Calafiori was often out of position in the left-back slot and Pedro Neto could cut in on his left foot. That seemed to be the sacrifice that Arteta was prepared to make in keeping the hammer on Chelsea. If Neto had not struck the post in one such escape in time added on at the end of the first half it might have been different.

Ødegaard struck what would be the winner early in the first half, and although Chelsea fizzed enough in the later stages it always felt as though it was Arsenal’s game. Raya came into his own in the 89th minute when Estêvão, a substitute, cut in from the right and hit a fierce shot that the goalkeeper pushed over. It was close in some ways – and in others not at all.

“It hurts. It hurts because a defeat has to hurt. It has been a very intense game with different moments for everything. We had chances to equalise. In the first half as well a couple of chances. Never happy if you lose.

“After we scored, there were 15-20 minutes where we had to defend too much and we were struggling a bit to get control. We then had better spells with the ball. Overall, it was a very tight, very intense game. We could do better with the second goal to conceded too early. The guys gave everything, tried everything. It has to hurt.

“It is about preparing the best possible way to compete the best possible way. You need to control the overloads on the right side. It is part of the game to have these actions. We continue. It is game three and this is going to be a long, long ride.”

"That's not sustainable" Daniel Sturridge reflects Chelsea's performance after the 2-1 defeat to Arsenal 💭 pic.twitter.com/3EMx88QLA0

"He's not the goalkeeper that won the World Cup" 🏆Jamie Carragher says Emi Martinez is not as quick or sharp as he once was 🧤 pic.twitter.com/SOp4XhoYIr

“I think the worrying thing for everybody else already is that [William] Saliba, who is genuinely world-class arguably, probably the best centre-back in world football, has not played a minute of football so far this season. And it does not look like anyone can score against them.

“There is a massive gulf between both teams; their XIs and the squads. It will take Chelsea a while to get to that level, if they can get there. But I thought Arsenal were fantastic today. We do not normally see Arsenal in these games, end-to-end, because they very rarely go behind. They are so strong defensively they do not need to get involved in those games.

“They still did not look like they were going to give too much away, even though they were bombing forwards and putting so many bodies in the opposition box.”

“It was a massive game with a tough opponent. It was really hard for us; we got there in the end. Our mentality is to keep fighting. Conceding early was not ideal but we reacted really well. We played well in the second half and got our reward. We showed our quality today. The result reflected that.”

“He is a really smart player and moves so well. He takes defenders attention. When he makes the run and I come from behind I am always free. It was a brilliant goal.”

“We knew Arsenal were the better team and they have proven that in this game. The question before today was, how close are Chelsea? And [Xabi] Alonso will be proud of what he has seen. There are obviously improvements to be made, but they gave it a right good go. A lot of very good things and they will be frustrated and disappointed, but they may potentially look back on this game as a good moment rather than as bad as it may feel right now.”

Possession: Arsenal 55%-45% ChelseaShots: 16-13Shots on target: 9-5Corners: 5-3Touches in opposition box: 44-25

The final whistle is blown at the Emirates and Arsenal maintain their 100% record through three games as they have beaten Chelsea 2-1. They were 1-0 down inside the opening two minutes but goals from Havertz and Odegaard have led them to victory. Chelsea suffer their first competitive defeat under Xabi Alonso.

Pedro’s cross from the right has too much on it and Chavarria cannot head it back across goal. Chelsea’s last chance might have been that Estevao effort which was brilliantly saved by Raya.

That is a stunning save from Raya that may have preserved Arsenal’s victory. Estevao cuts in from the right and curls one towards the top corner. It looks set for the net but somehow Raya makes a fantastic save to deny Estevao.

Chelsea are bringing on Welbeck for Rogers, who is jeered by the Arsenal fans. Welbeck comes on with a note, that he gives to his captain James.

Arsenal have lost a bit of their composure and structure. I suspect that’s why Arteta has turned to Mikel Merino. He screamed at his bench immediately after a messy passage of play, and Merino emerged about 20 seconds later. Merino is very much the “sensible adult” sort of player, who should calm things down. Although he hasn’t yet.

England team-mates Declan Rice and Morgan Rogers were really going at it there. Rogers absolutely furious with Rice tripping him up. “You should have signed for a big club,” sing the Arsenal fans at Rogers...

It has kicked off. Rogers is cynically tripped by Rice but the referee somehow does not see it. Rogers is incensed and marches over to Rice, who has massively got away with one there. Rice knew exactly what he was doing as he deliberately trips Rogers. That is a nasty from Rice, who avoids a booking, yet Rogers is shown a yellow card. That is frankly dreadful refereeing.

"He's FUMING Morgan Rogers!" 😳 pic.twitter.com/FciivEedvh

Estevao is brought on for Chelsea in place of Neto.

Pedro wins a corner off Gabriel out on the left in front of the travelling Chelsea fans. Gusto’s delivery to the back post is caught at the second attempt by Raya.

Double change for Arsenal as Gyokeres and Merino come on for Havertz and Odegaard.

Gusto’s cross from the right is put behind by Konsa for a Chelsea corner out on the right. Neto clips it in but Arsenal head away. James then opts to shoot from range and his effort is blocked by Gabriel. That shot looked to be going on target but Raya may have had it covered anyway.

Rice’s corner from the left is flicked on by Havertz at the near post and the last touch comes off James for another Arsenal corner on the other side. Arsenal take it short and fell to get into the danger zone but do win themselves another corner.

Saka delivers it into a dangerous area and the ball is flicked, looking like it is going into the Chelsea net, but Martinez makes the save whilst on the ground.

Havertz plays a first-time flick into the path of Saka, whose first-time effort looking for the far corner is saved well by Martinez to his right.

Odegaard feeds a clever pass into the Chelsea penalty area to pick out Zubimendi, whose shot is blocked.

Double change for Arsenal as Zubimendi and Hincapie replace Lewis-Skelly and Calafiori.

Palmer gets a shot away from the right side of the box but it is straight at Raya. Chelsea are just starting to wrestle back some momentum.

Gusto has only just come on but has a chance. The ball is laid to him on the edge of the box and he hits it first time but his effort goes over the bar.

The momentum is certainly with Arsenal right now so Xabi Alonso is making a double change. Gusto and Chavarria replace Lavia and Hato. With Gusto coming on for Lavia, Chelsea do not actually have any out-and-out central midfielders on the pitch.

Tzolis is the first Arsenal player into the book today. He is brought down by Lacroix and then demands that the Chelsea defender be booked, waving an imaginary card, and is then shown a yellow himself. Lacroix was also booked for the original foul.

Two former teammates challenge each other as Konsa slides in to make a perfectly-timed challenge on Rogers. The home crowd loved that tackle from Konsa, who won that tackle fair and square.

Chelsea made Odegaard angry about two minutes before that goal. The Arsenal captain, who is a mild-mannered guy, was really unhappy with a tackle by James. They were exchanging some verbals afterwards, before Odegaard then ran away from James to score.

That’s five goals Chelsea have conceded in just over a game-and-a-half since Emi Martinez took over in goal. In fairness, that Odegaard goal wasn’t his fault.

Arsenal were forced to respond when Chelsea scored early but now it is on the visitors to see how they respond after falling behind.

For the first time this afternoon, Arsenal lead and it is a quality goal. Tzolis receives it out on the left and cuts inside onto his right. He plays the ball inside towards Havertz, who is in space on the edge of the Chelsea box. It is really intelligent from Havertz, who dummies it to take away Fofana and allows the ball to run through to Odegaard, who takes one touch before firing past Martinez.

"A spear through the heart of Chelsea!" Martin Odegaard puts Arsenal in front at the Emirates 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5deEQykjck

Arsenal just scored the same goal they scored against Manchester City in the Community Shield. Tzolis into Odegaard, low and fast.

As it stands, Manchester City will be the only team with a 100% record after three games.

I think Chelsea are now 19 Premier League games without keeping a clean sheet, dating back to last season.

A few Chelsea players were having a moan at referee Christopher Kavanagh as they went off for half-time. But Alonso’s players need to calm down and keep their cool. There were signs the Blues’ old disciplinary problems could rear their head again with Joao Pedro and Cole Palmer being booked. Romeo Lavia also squared up to Ben White for no real reason. Chelsea have to keep 11 players on the pitch.

Possession: Arsenal 58%-42% ChelseaShots: 10-6Shots on target: 6-3Corners: 2-0Touches in opposition box: 26-13

A really enjoyable half of football, even if it was slowed down a little in the last few minutes by a series of niggly fouls. Arsenal are the better team here but Chelsea are definitely dangerous. That Neto shot off the post was evidence of how quickly they can hurt the Arsenal defence.

The first half is brought to an end and it is 1-1 going into the break at the Emirates.

Chelsea hit the post late on in the half. Chelsea counter from inside their own half and Pedro whips a ball first time down the right channel to pick out the run of Neto. The Portuguese forward drives at Gabriel inside the Arsenal box and cuts inside onto his preferred left foot. His effort comes back off the far post and Chelsea were inches away from retaking the lead.

That left side of the Arsenal defence again. Wide open for Neto to run into the space. Chelsea looking for the early ball every time.

Tensions are boiling over as Lavia and White come to blows. As Lavia shepherds the ball out of play, White threw himself to ground and wanted a free-kick. Lavia is not impressed by White’s antics and lets him know about it.

Is Palmer in some trouble? Raya catches a free-kick into his box and gets Arsenal going on the counter with a long ball forward. With Havertz getting away from him, Palmer brings him down and takes the yellow. There was another covering defender, hence why it was just a yellow.

As we approach half-time, there have been 15 shots in total from both sides in the game with nine of those being on target.

Chelsea win it just inside the Arsenal half after good defensive work from Lavia and Pedro then spots Raya off his line. The Chelsea forward therefore opts to shoot from a long way out but drags his effort wide.

White and Havertz exchange a neat one-two down Arsenal’s right, with the latter clipping the ball to the back post. Lavia, with Saka right behind him, heads away well under pressure.

That is a decent opportunity for Rogers to get his second of the game. Pedro lays it off to him on the left side of the box and Rogers tries to curl one into the far corner but it goes wide.

Tremendous game at the Emirates. Both teams attacking one another. Chelsea have a lot of space with Pedro Neto on the right and keep using that diagonal ball. Once again, though, they look suspect in defence. The Havertz equaliser could have been stopped twice, but Chelsea defence just did not react. Fofana let Havertz past and Odegaard set a bit of a screen that stopped Lacroix getting close.

Former Chelsea player scores against former Arsenal goalkeeper. Interesting reaction from the Arsenal players to that Havertz goal: most of them ran straight back to their own half. They want to get on with this game. Suggests they can sense Chelsea’s vulnerability.

Against his former club, Havertz gets the equaliser but again there will be an offside check. It appears he is onside as he receives the ball on the right. Havertz then drives across the face of the penalty area and shoots towards the near post. Martinez should make the save but can only palm it into the corner of the net. The goal stands and it is 1-1 at the Emirates.

A precise finish from Kai Havertz and Arsenal are level! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DqL1MEX4zN

I think we’d be talking about Robert Sanchez if he had let that Havertz shot in at his near post. That wasn’t great from Martinez and Arsenal fans will love reminding him of it. Great game, this.

James decides to shoot from range and he strikes it really well, forcing Raya into a good save. Arsenal then counter and it ends with Odegaard having a shot blocked. Should Havertz have shot himself rather than lay it off for Odegaard?

Back come Chelsea and Pedro nearly gets on the end of a cross from Palmer.

Palmer, who has been quiet so far, receives it on the edge of the box and he is afforded too much space. He decides to shoot and looks to curl it into the far corner but Raya gets down to his right to make the save. He had to make sure he did not spill it as Pedro was lurking.

Tzolis cross from the left having been found by a great ball from Odegaard finds Havertz near the edge of the box. Fofana makes a crucial block to deny Havertz but Arsenal have the corner out on the left. Once more, Chelsea leave plenty of players up the pitch and Fofana heads away.

Odegaard works it to Saka on the right side of the box and the latter strikes towards goal, forcing Martinez into a decent save.

The goal will not stand. Konsa was offside before Calafiori scored so Chelsea remain 1-0 up.

#ARSCHE – 12' VAR OVERTURNVAR checked the referee's call of goal – and determined that Konsa was in an offside position in the build-up and recommended that the goal was disallowed.

The hosts equalise with a set-piece. Pedro should clear Rice’s free-kick but completely misses it. The ball comes to Gabriel, whose shot is saved by Martinez. Konsa then hits the post before a mad scramble ensues. Calafiori then forces the ball into the net. However, VAR are checking the goal...

Hato brings Saka down not far outside the Chelsea penalty area and both Odegaard and Rice are standing over it. Chelsea have just three men in the wall. Rice is going to take...

Arsenal have a corner out on the right yet Chelsea, who are the ones defending, leave four players up the pitch rather than in their own box. Is that madness or a masterstroke? The delivery from Saka goes beyond the back post, where it is then headed back across goal. Saka gets to it and then goes down but he was offside anyway.

It looked like Chelsea left four attackers upfield for that Arsenal corner. That’s one way of reducing the traffic in the six-yard box.

Chelsea have now scored inside the first five minutes of each of their three Premier League games this season. Has that ever happened before? Thanks OptaJoe:

3 - Chelsea are the first side to score in the opening five minutes of three successive Premier League games since Newcastle United in December 2024, and first ever to do so in their first three matches of a season in the competition.Blocks. pic.twitter.com/g9bum6fQkA

Fofana brings down Havertz with a rather silly challenge and Arsenal have a free-kick out on the right, with the chance to send it into the Chelsea box. Odegaard drills it low in towards the near post and picks out the run of Calafiori. The Italian’s effort is saved by Martinez’s legs and then a mad scramble for the ball ensues. It is difficult to see where the ball is and ends up going out for a goal kick. Martinez stays down and is receiving treatment to his head. It comes as a result of Gabriel’s boot flying into Martinez’s head. Should VAR be taking a look at that one? They clear it but Gabriel might count himself lucky that a review for violent conduct was not called.

Not even two minutes into the game, Chelsea take the lead and it is a man Arsenal wanted over the summer who scores against them. Rogers, on the edge of the Arsenal penalty area, watches the ball onto his foot and volleys first time into the bottom left corner. A fine finish from Rogers and Chelsea have the perfect start. How will Arsenal respond?

Morgan Rogers fires Chelsea in front inside TWO minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/ca8cqnT2Wm

The first goal Arsenal concede this season is scored by the first player they wanted to sign in the summer.

Wow. That had echoes of Eze scoring against Tottenham last season. Just as Spurs had missed out to Arsenal for Eze, Arsenal missed out to Chelsea for Rogers. So what happens? Of course, he scores. After just two minutes. I’m also pretty sure Rogers imitated the Thierry Henry celebration next to the corner flag just to rub salt into Arsenal’s wounds.

The two bosses, who have known each other since they were children, share a warm embrace before kick-off.

We are under way at the Emirates. Both sides have 100% records coming into this one but at least one of those will fall today.

Perhaps some early mind games from Arsenal as Chelsea were left waiting in the tunnel for a little while before Arsenal eventually emerged. Eventually both sides emerge from the tunnel and we are moments away from kick-off at the Emirates. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this afternoon:

Arsenal: Raya; White, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Rice, Lewis-Skelly, Odegaard; Saka, Havertz, Tzolis.Substitutes: Kepa, Hincapie, Eze, Gyokeres, Madueke, Merino, Zubimendi, Guimaraes, Dowman.

Chelsea: Martinez; Acheampong, Lacroix, Fofana; Neto, James, Lavia, Hato; Palmer, Pedro, Rogers.Substitutes: Penders, Colwill, Gusto, Chavarriia, Barco, Quenda, Gittens, Estevao, Welbeck.

"It's a London derby, it's two big clubs"Mikel Arteta speaks as Arsenal host Chelsea on Super Sunday ⚔️ pic.twitter.com/S4x7Vx3dvV

"We need to play with maturity, with intelligence" 🧠Xabi Alonso speaks ahead of Chelsea's visit to Arsenal 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/Y2egodgmY5

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso has confirmed that the Ecuadorian midfielder was close but Alonso says it was not worth the risk at this stage of the season. He also confirmed that Levi Colwill being on the bench today was down to fitness.

The first game of the afternoon has just concluded at the Hill Dickinson and Everton have snatched a point at the death against Manchester United, with Ainsley Maitland-Niles scoring a screamer on his Everton debut with almost the last kick of the game to make it 2-2. You can follow the reaction to that game right here.

INS:Marco Palestra ⇠ Atalanta, £42mMorgan Rogers ⇠ Aston Villa, £117mMaxence Lacroix ⇠ Crystal Palace, £51mDanny Welbeck ⇠ Brighton, UndisclosedJordan Henderson ⇠ Brentford, FreeEmi Martinez ⇠ Aston Villa, £7.5m

OUTS:Andrey Santos ⇢ Manchester United, £50mMarc Cucurella ⇢ Real Madrid, £50mTrevoh Chalobah ⇢ Como, £30mLiam Delap ⇢ Nottingham Forest, £50mNicolas Jackson ⇢ Aston Villa, £65mEnzo Fernandez ⇢ Manchester City, £125m

Chelsea fans, how would you rate your window out of 10? Have your say in the comments section at the bottom of the blog.

It is not always particularly significant when a manager says his player can be one of the best in the world. But it is probably worth taking notice when Xabi Alonso articulates his belief that Reece James can be one of the best midfielders on the planet.

For Liverpool, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich and Spain, Alonso was one of the finest midfielders of his generation and also played with some of the best midfielders in the world. So the Chelsea manager knows a thing or two about what it takes.

James has long been considered – when fit – one of the best right-backs in the world. But it had already been evident before the final 24 hours of the transfer window that the Chelsea player would spend a lot of time in midfield under Alonso.

Arsenal fans, did your club do enough during the transfer window? If not, what would you have liked to have seen your club get? Have your say in he comments section at the bottom of the blog.

"We have a good chemistry"João Pedro on his relationship with Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers 🤝 pic.twitter.com/eIwCL9joPg

Bukayo Saka has arrived at a career crossroads. We will soon learn whether he is destined to be a good Arsenal player or if he will elevate himself to the level of Premier League, Champions League and England great.

This weekend Saka turns 25, an age when footballers typically enter their peak. Although his legendary status at Arsenal is secure as a title winner, the reaction to the champions’ transfer window suggests there is a general feeling that he can and should produce more to earn “world class” status.

Mikel Arteta is short of such an attacker. He spent the summer investigating whether players of Vinícius Júnior and Julián Alvarez’s calibre might add much-needed stardust to his front three. Failure to secure a big-name forward has led many to conclude that Arsenal’s title defence will be in the mould of their impressive, but cautious 1-0 victory at Aston Villa.

"It's another tough game"Ben White on coming up against Chelsea's front three 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/gfazGGNSA8

It is a relationship that Arteta has previously described as “deeper than just a friendship”. It started with skateboards and sand, as they made the daily journey to the beach to play tennis and football, and continued into their adult lives. When Alonso was playing for Liverpool and Arteta for Everton, there was a time when they both had flats on the fourth floor of the same building in the Albert Dock.

It is extraordinary that these two individuals – born just a few months apart – now find themselves in positions of such significance in English football. But it is not a coincidence. Throughout their lives, they have driven each other forward.

“This kid, he was maybe even crazier than me about football,” Alonso once said of Arteta and their shared childhood. “He was a little bit younger than me and my friends – just a few months maybe. But you know how you always push your ‘little friends’ at that age? Well, we tried, but he was a competitive monster.”

Arsenal: Raya; White, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Rice, Lewis-Skelly, Odegaard; Saka, Havertz, Tzolis.Substitutes: Kepa, Hincapie, Eze, Gyokeres, Madueke, Merino, Zubimendi, Guimaraes, Dowman.

How chaotic will Arsenal allow the game to become today? Both of Chelsea’s league matches this season have been remarkably open, to the point of silliness. Arsenal do not usually allow such things to happen on their watch. They are far too sensible for that. But, having seen Brighton create so many chances at Stamford Bridge last week, Arteta may fancy his team to do some serious damage to Chelsea’s damage if the match opens up.

There’s a slight surprise in Chelsea’s line-up with Levi Colwill dropping to the bench and Josh Acheampong coming in. That could point to Alonso changing to a back four with Acheampong at right-back and Pedro Neto playing further forwards as a right winger. Chelsea only managed 25 per cent of possession against Brighton, so is this an attempt to get more of the ball? As expected, Moises Caicedo is not fit so Reece James and Romeo Lavia will need to play well.

Your Chelsea XI.#CFC | #ARSCHE pic.twitter.com/UkSmiUVgO3

A personal opinion that no one asked for: Arsenal should have signed Joao Pedro last summer, when the Brazilian joined Chelsea for £60m. Arsenal bought Viktor Gyokeres instead, in a deal that could ultimately be more expensive, and there is no doubt which forward offers more to their team. Joao Pedro always seemed to cause problems for Arsenal’s defence when he played against them during his time at Brighton, and he has a flexibility and versatility that would have been perfect for Arteta’s system. Arsenal had twice explored the possibility of signing him over the years. It is surely a source of regret that they never became serious about it. So far this season, Joao Pedro has scored and assisted in both league games. Gyokeres, by contrast, has played zero minutes.

They have just got back under way in the second half on Merseyside and Manchester United have taken the lead against Everton through Bryan Mbeumo. You can follow the action from the Hill Dickinson here.

Will Ezri Konsa come into Arsenal’s starting lineup today? It would be harsh on Cristhian Mosquera, who has been excellent so far this season, but when you pay more than £50m for a ready-made, elite-level centre-back, these are the matches you surely want him for. Mosquera had a slight injury against Aston Villa on Monday night, which may give Arteta the perfect reason to throw his new signing into the side.

Saturday:Newcastle 2 Bournemouth 2Brentford 1 Sunderland 1Brighton 1 Leeds 1Fulham 2 Crystal Palace 3Manchester City 1 Coventry 0Nottingham Forest 0 Tottenham 0Hull City 0 Aston Villa 0

Today:Everton 0 Manchester United 0 HTArsenal vs Chelsea 4.30pm

Mikel Arteta insists Arsenal are “better equipped” for success this season, despite falling short in their attempts to add a top-class attacker. Arsenal have allowed four forward players to leave this summer and brought in one, Greece winger Christos Tzolis.

The departures of Gabriel Martinelli, Leandro Trossard, Gabriel Jesus and Ethan Nwaneri (on loan) have raised concerns among supporters that the champions lack firepower. Moves for Morgan Rogers, Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez did not come to fruition. Arteta, though, feels Arsenal are stronger now than at the end of last season following a summer in which they added midfielder Bruno Guimarães and defender Ezri Konsa.

“We are better equipped,” said Arteta, who faces Rogers and close friend Xabi Alonso. “We have more players available than the start of last season. We have increased the quality and we have increased the leadership, which is very important.”

Asked specifically about the attack, he added: “Yeah, but that’s another question. We have to prove in that particular position whether we are better or not. Let’s see. We need to play. I don’t like to make assumptions.

“It’s not just the responsibility of those players, it’s the team and the dynamic. We have multiple options to play there with different profiles. It’s human nature. When you talk to people and you ask: ‘Ok, what is on your bucket list?’ Sometimes we forget the reverse bucket list, which are the things you already have that are incredible. It’s very important to value what we have, what we have created together. The ambition is great, but [don’t] lose perspective to what we already have which is amazing.”

Two sides with 100% records meet in a London derby in north London as defending champions Arsenal host Chelsea at the Emirates. Arsenal have wins over Coventry and Aston Villa to their name whilst Chelsea have beaten Fulham and Brighton.

Arsenal could make it three wins from three to start the season, a feat they have only achieved once in the last 21 seasons. They have lost just one of their last 29 Premier League London derbies. Mikel Arteta comes up against his childhood friend Xabi Alonso today.

“Really happy for him [Alonso],” Arteta said. “It is incredible because obviously we have the history we have together, the same with Andoni [Iraola]. To be facing each other at such a level and with the responsibility we have managing some of the top clubs in the country is a really beautiful thing to experience. Now it will be tougher to meet because of the schedule we both have but that friendship will go for many years. We shared some great moments but now it is the competition and when you face each other, you know what happens.”

Chelsea were involved in late drama on transfer deadline day. They were on the verge of signing midfielder Lamine Camara from Monaco only to see that deal fall through at the last minute. After being linked with a move away throughout the summer, Chelsea did in the end sell Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City for a joint Premier League transfer record fee of £125m.

“In football, many things happen and you need to be prepared for everything,” Chelsea boss Alonso said. “With Enzo, we have had conversations, but always with respect for what he has done for the club. It has been great, we are thankful, but it is time to move forward. We take all the decisions together. We are responsible for them, we work together with every decision, big and small.

“We knew that, ultimately, the last goal is to have the best for the team, the best for the squad, the best for daily work here. We want to build a good spirit, a good team, and we have always taken decisions thinking we want to reach that. We have the squad we have. We have a lot of big personalities, players with a lot of quality in all the different positions, different lines and now we are ready to go.”

Arsenal won this fixture 2-1 last season, with William Saliba and Jurrien Timber earning Mikel Arteta’s side three points on their way to the title. Arsenal are unbeaten in their last nine Premier League matches against Chelsea.

#1750. Liverpool transfer news: New Alexis Mac Allister contract timeline given as two-year claim made (exclusive)

By Ben Knapton | 23 Nov 2026 13:45

Liverpool are unlikely to give any consideration to a new contract for Alexis Mac Allister before February, Reds Champions League winner Didi Hamann has exclusively told Sports Mole.

The Argentina international is in the last two years of his current contract with Liverpool, having not signed a single extension since joining from Brighton & Hove Albion in the summer of 2023.

Mac Allister revealed in September that Liverpool were not in a position to offer him a new contract, after the 27-year-old experienced a noticeable decline in individual performance levels in 2025-26.

However, after a positive World Cup with Argentina, Mac Allister has returned to form for Liverpool, scoring five goals and providing one assist in 17 appearances across all competitions so far this season.

The midfielder has started nine of Liverpool's 11 Premier League games under Andoni Iraola and also performed well in Sunday's 4-0 win over Manchester United, creating two chances, completing 89% of his passes and winning four of his five ground duels.

Nevertheless, ex-Liverpool midfielder Hamann does not believe that talks over a new deal will begin for another three months, and any extension is only likely to be two years at best.

"They said to him there's no contract now, and he's in his late 20s," Hamann told Sports Mole when asked if Mac Allister had already played his way into a new contract.

"If he carries on performing, if he keeps on scoring goals, then come February, March, April, there might be a time where you say. 'maybe we keep him another two years.' But I don't think there's any rush at the moment."

Mac Allister - who turns 28 on December 24 - has come up with 24 goals and 21 assists in 167 matches for Liverpool since 2023, and he earns £180,000 a week under his current contract terms, according to Capology.

The Argentine's reported salary only makes him the 11th highest-paid player at Liverpool, below new signing Ronald Araujo (£210k) and almost half of what Virgil van Dijk earns (£350k).

Mac Allister's relationship with Ryan Gravenberch blossomed to the maximum in the 2024-25 season, culminating in both midfielders becoming Premier League champions for the first time.

However, Mac Allister's decline from a defensive and box-to-box standpoint was striking; compared to 2024-25, he made 45% fewer tackles and 26% fewer recoveries than in the 2025-26 campaign.

Gravenberch's own form did not help the South American's cause, though, and the latter has had a rejuvenated look about him since the World Cup, immediately earning Iraola's trust in the process.

Mac Allister's availability remains exceptional too, as he has only missed 11 matches for club and country since joining Liverpool and has been involved in every match so far this season.

With Wataru Endo almost certainly on the way out and James McConnell still on the fringes, Liverpool should speed up the process of tying down Mac Allister, lest they risk losing another midfield option in 2027.

Didi Hamann was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of Lottoland Live Casino.

#1749. Palace docked three points for substitution rule breach in Everton victory

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Crystal Palace have been deducted three points for breaching substitution rules during their 1-0 win over Everton on the opening day of the Women's Super League.

Lexi Lloyd-Smith scored the only goal at The 360 Engage Stadium in September, but the Eagles have since had those points removed after using too many substitution windows.

The introduction of Kirsty Howat in the 97th minute was Palace's fourth separate change, with other substitutions taking place in the 62nd, 83rd and 90th minutes.

While WSL managers are allowed to make five changes in a game, they must be made across only three stoppages in play to avoid excessive time-wasting.

An independent tribunal determined that the breach was "inadvertent" and that it was "not intended to secure an unfair advantage," but added that a sporting sanction was "necessary."

The deduction means Palace drop to 13th in the WSL and behind Birmingham City on goal difference, after the Eagles were thumped 5-1 by London City Lionesses on Sunday.

Crystal Palace have been informed of the decision by a panel to agree to the WSL’s recommendation to deduct three points from our 2026/27 Barclays Women’s Super League tally, following the 97th-minute substitution that used a ‘fourth’ window in our recent fixture against Everton. https://t.co/aNpga6nt4C

— Crystal Palace F.C. Women (@cpfc_w) November 24, 2026

The Everton match was one of only two WSL games Palace had won this season, and the Eagles said they were "disappointed" by the outcome.

"Everyone at the club is obviously frustrated that such a minor infraction, given that the player was on the pitch for only 46 seconds while the ball was in play, has led to such a significant penalty – a penalty which we do not agree is reasonable or proportionate," Palace's statement read.

"We are disappointed for the players and staff who worked so hard to secure a deserved victory on our return to the WSL."

#1748. Manchester United learn Leny Yoro red card appeal verdict after controversial suspension

Leny Yoro will be available for Manchester United’s Premier League meeting with Brentford this weekend after his one-match suspension was struck off on appeal.

The centre-back was dismissed after just eight minutes as United visited Liverpool on Sunday for a clumsy tackle on Alexander Isak.

The Swede was through one-on-one with Senne Lammens and took a heavy first touch before being caught by the backtracking Yoro, just outside the box. Dominik Szoboszlai scored the opener from the resultant free-kick and United ultimately lost 4-0.

United were quick to appeal the decision, which new head coach Mauricio Pochettino and a number of his players questioned in post-match media duties.

And their appeal has been upheld, meaning Yoro will be available this weekend for the visit of Brentford to Old Trafford.

A statement from the FA read: Leny Yoro’s one-match suspension has been removed following a claim of wrongful dismissal. The Manchester United player was sent off for denying an obvious goal scoring opportunity during their Premier League match against Liverpool on Sunday 22 November.”

Speaking post-match, United captain Fernandes questioned the decision to send Yoro off, saying Isak drew the foul and was not in control of the ball anyway.

“We have four officials at the game, plus another two on VAR. I understand it’s a difficult situation, but VAR can watch it again and again, with replays, slow motion, everything,” he told ESPN Brasil.

“Isak puts his leg in front of Leny simply to try to win a foul. The ball is knocked forward, towards Senne’s hands. He has absolutely no control of the ball.

“For me, fine, it’s a foul. But you can’t send him off because there’s no control of the ball. It’s not a situation where Isak is going one-on-one with the goalkeeper. So I think the punishment was a bit harsh on Leny.”

Pochettino echoed his complaints, adding: “The ball was for the goalkeeper. In that situation, if you review the VAR you can see for sure, he never had the intention to connect with Isak.

“When the control was long with the striker, the ball was going to the goalkeeper, he runs and goes down. In Leny's case, it wasn't intentional. It was an unusual situation that is normal, everyone who plays football can feel it.”

#1745. Man Utd make decision on what to do next after Leny Yoro's controversial red card against Liverpool

By Saikat Mandal | 23 Nov 2026 13:57, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 14:51

Manchester United have reportedly notified the FA of their intention to appeal Leny Yoro's red card.

The centre-back was sent off during Man Utd's 4-0 defeat against Liverpool at Anfield in the Premier League on Sunday after bringing down Alexander Isak as the striker raced through on goal.

The Red Devils were reduced to 10 men just eight minutes into the contest, a moment that significantly altered the complexion of the game as Liverpool enjoyed greater possession and created better opportunities.

While Man Utd could arguably have done more to frustrate the Reds, there is little doubt that Yoro's dismissal had a major bearing on the outcome.

According to Sky Sports, the Red Devils intend to appeal Yoro's dismissal, with Mauricio Pochettino offering his interpretation of the incident after the game.

The main point of contention is whether the foul constituted a clear denial of an obvious goalscoring opportunity, with questions surrounding whether Isak was actually in control of the ball.

Under the laws of the game, one of the considerations when determining whether a player should be sent off for Denying an Obvious Goal-Scoring Opportunity (DOGSO) is whether the attacking player had control of the ball.

Pochettino not only questioned that aspect of the decision but also highlighted the referee's failure to penalise Jeremy Jacquet for his challenge on Bryan Mbeumo at the opposite end just moments earlier.

It remains to be seen how the FA will assess the incidents, although former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher has backed the on-field decisions in both cases.

Unless the decision is overturned following an appeal, Yoro is set to serve a one-match domestic suspension rather than a three-match ban, as his denial of a obvious goalscoring opportunity was a non-violent offence.

While the defender is available to face Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League on Wednesday, he will miss Man United's next Premier League fixture at home to Brentford on Saturday.

Yoro will then be available to return to Premier League action on December 2 when Pochettino's side travel to St James' Park to take on Newcastle United.

The Red Devils are now without a win in their last nine Premier League matches and have slipped to 19th in the table, with only Crystal Palace faring worse.

#1744. Luca Williams-Barnett signs new Tottenham contract after stellar full debut

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Tottenham wonderkid Luca Williams-Barnett has signed a new contract, tying his long-term future to his boyhood club.

The 18-year-old was in the final two years of his existing contract, but has now agreed fresh terms.

Much has been expected of Williams-Barnett for quite some time, after impressing at both domestic and international youth levels with Spurs and England, and he has had to be patient after being given his senior debut last season in the Carabao Cup aged just 16 years old.

Two short cameos in the Premier League earlier this season led to a first senior start on Saturday for the visit of Ipswich, in which the teenager produced a star performance with a goal and assist in a 2-0 win.

Williams-Barnett became Tottenham’s youngest scorer in the Premier League since Gareth Bale in 2007 when putting Spurs ahead after just 15 minutes, before turning provider to set up Dominic Solanke shortly after half-time.

Reacting to the man-of-the-match performance, which earned the youngster a standing ovation from the home crowd, Roberto De Zerbi compared the 18-year-old to Barcelona star Lamine Yamal.

"I’m positive about that because he has great confidence. He knows all his qualities, but I think he has a very good family and it’s crucial for this type of player," De Zerbi said.

"I think he’s already in a top club. He has nothing to change because he’s already at the top of the level of the club he wants to arrive. He understands because he’s smart. He’s smart to understand the behaviour.

"I think I’m positive about his behaviour, his character, because I’ve been working with him for three or four months and I know him enough to say this."

De Zerbi said: "When I said the first 11 to the players, I said, ‘remember the first game, the debut of you, and help the kid tomorrow, because he’s one of us, and if he plays well, we have more chances to win the game.’”

#1743. Man City charges: Jeremy Doku's response to “juicy” discussion on guilty Premier League verdict

By Oliver Thomas | 23 Nov 2026 13:59

Jeremy Doku was the latest Manchester City player to be questioned on his thoughts regarding the club’s Premier League financial charges case during a press conference on Monday.

An independent commission has found Man City guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules and the majority of charges in relation to its failure to co-operate with the investigation.

In a verdict delivered at the end of September, the Citizens are accused of using "sham" contracts with a number of commercial partners to disguise secret funding of more than £830m and artificially inflate revenues between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 campaigns.

Man City have repeatedly expressed their innocence and lodged an appeal last month, stating that “a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case.”

Should Man City’s guilty verdict be upheld, the club would be in danger of a plethora of possible sanctions, including heavy fines, transfer bans, stripping titles, points deductions leading to relegation and expulsion from the Premier League.

On the pitch, Man City have recently suffered a dip in form, failing to win any of their last four Premier League games (D1 L3), but manager Enzo Maresca played down suggestions that the 115 charges case is distracting his players - something Didi Hamann disagrees with.

Since September’s verdict, the likes of captain Ruben Dias and star striker Erling Haaland have faced questions on the ongoing legal case, and Doku is now the latest City star to be asked for his views on the matter.

However, Doku politely declined to comment on the club’s situation and was keen to discuss on-field matters only when speaking to the media ahead of City’s Champions League clash with Napoli on Tuesday.

“I know this is all juicy for you guys, but we have a big week; Napoli tomorrow, and then Arsenal," the Belgium international told reporters on Monday.

"So I think there's enough to speak about there instead of speaking about the charges. I'm not the person to speak about the charges, so with all respect I don't really want to be on that topic. We can speak about football, that's no problem."

In August, just a month before the guilty verdict was published, Doku extended his contract with Man City until the summer of 2031, and the winger has no regrets over his decision.

"I signed because I was happy to sign. I didn't think about anything else,” Doku clearly stated after being asked whether the charges came into his conversations over a new contract.

"I don't think it was a difficult thing for me. When you look at this club, how big of a club it is, the trophies they won and everything, it was an easy choice for me.

"I was happy here, I am happy here, I have a wife here, a son, it was an easy choice for me. So I didn't think a lot, obviously everything needed to be right for me to sign, but as soon as everything was right on both sides, it was an easy choice for me."

Assessing Man City’s season so far from an individual and collective perspective, Doku added: "I think I can do better. I started off with an injury this season, then came back well.

“And then the team, we did well with the first seven [Premier League] games where we won, and afterwards it was a bit more tough. As everyone knows, at the moment it's a bit more difficult, but I'm sure we'll bounce back, me as well."

Doku is a strong contender to start for Man City in their Champions League clash against Napoli, with the Citizens seeking to move one step closer to automatic last-16 qualification having already won three of their first four League Phase matches.

Maresca, meanwhile, has provided a positive update on the fitness of right-back Matheus Nunes, who missed the 1-1 Premier League draw with Fulham last weekend.

#1741. PSG’s Champions League ‘obsession’ cost them league title under Tuchel, says Florenzi

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Former Paris Saint-Germain defender Alessandro Florenzi believes their "obsession" with winning the Champions League cost them the Ligue 1 title under Thomas Tuchel.

Florenzi spent the 2020-21 season on loan at PSG, who lost in the Champions League final to Bayern Munich in the previous campaign.

Tuchel won 74.8% of his games in charge of PSG (G127 W95 D13 L19), his best win percentage at any club, and led them to back-to-back titles in 2018-19 and 2019-20, but things unravelled the following season.

PSG sacked Tuchel in December 2020 after they were falling behind in the Ligue 1 title race to Lille, who would go on to win the league by one point.

It was only the second season since 2012-13 in which PSG failed to win the league title, after Monaco won the French top-flight in 2016-17.

However, Tuchel was hired by Chelsea a month after being sacked by PSG and went on to win the Champions League with the Blues in that same season.

Florenzi described Tuchel's Champions League win as "karma", but the Italian was not surprised to see PSG eventually win the competition.

"At the time, PSG hadn't won the Champions League yet, but you could see the president wanted to build something big," Florenzi told L'Equipe.

Champions League eve at the PSG Campus!  #PSGRoma I #UCL https://t.co/qRAAgpBlQh

"Their obsession was the Champions League. And that's undoubtedly what cost us the league title; that season, we only thought about the Champions League.

"We lost in the semi-final against Manchester City, and Tuchel won it in the final. That's karma! But I have great memories of Paris, and I won my first trophies there.

"I told myself that PSG would end up winning the Champions League, yes, but something had to happen. And that something is Luis Enrique.

"With him, it's no longer the same club."

#1740. Millwall hit with partial stadium ban for discriminatory chanting

Millwall will play December’s match against Sheffield United under a partial stadium closure after being found guilty of “ableist and homophobic chanting” from supporters.

The FA’s regulatory commission proved breaches of FA rule E21, which regulates supporter misconduct, observed during last season’s clash with Charlton Athletic at The Den.

They were handed a two-game stadium ban as a result, though the second of those two matches is suspended.

Four blocks of the Dockers Stand will be closed for the visit of the Blades.

They have another partial stadium closure suspended until the end of next season, have been fined £70,000 and had an extended FA Action Plan applied.

A club statement read: “Both chants are discriminatory and offensive, and the club condemns them in the strongest possible terms.

“Ableist and homophobic chanting, as well as any other form of discriminatory chanting, has no place in football or society.

“Any individual identified as engaging in such abuse will face the consequences.

“The club will continue the significant work already achieved under its dedicated anti-discrimination campaign, ‘All ’Wall’, while continuously reviewing and enhancing best practice to ensure The Den is always a welcoming environment.”

#1738. Galatasaray vs. Aston Villa: Unai Emery claims unusual Champions League preparation 'will not be an excuse'

By Darren Plant | 23 Nov 2026 14:03

Unai Emery has played down the significance of Aston Villa's unusual preparations for Tuesday's Champions League fixture at Galatasaray.

Having put together a five-game winless streak, Emery is coming under more scrutiny than he usually receives at Villa Park.

Victory at Rams Park would effectively guarantee Villa a place in the top 24 of the League Phase table and a spot in the knockout stages.

However, Villa have been required to change from the standard routine for a Champions League away game due to the condition of Galatasaray's pitch.

Although the match is not at risk of being postponed, UEFA has informed Villa that they cannot train at RAMS Park before the game, and the Premier League club opted against taking up the option of training at a different Turkish location.

Instead, Villa conducted their final training session at their own training facilities, while Emery held his pre-match press conference in Birmingham rather than Istanbul.

The Spaniard insisted that the amended schedule cannot be used as "an excuse" if Villa do not earn a result versus the Super Lig champions.

He told reporters: "It's not changing our usual way. We prefer to train here at Bodymoor and then travel to the country.

"We are doing some exceptions when we are playing a long way with a time change, we are training in the country - we did it last year at Fenerbahce.

"Of course if we could train at the stadium maybe we would decide to, but it's not changing our routine.

"It's not an excuse because it's for both teams. We are ready and we are focused and analysing the opponent."

Not only do Villa face Galatasaray this week, they make the trip to play Ipswich Town on Saturday evening in a key Premier League match.

Villa remain with just three wins from 11 matches in England's top flight, and failure to prevail against either Galatasaray or Ipswich would leave Emery going seven matches without a win when he is due to sign a new contract.

While Emery has total backing from the club's hierarchy and supporters, it is clear he needs to end their current run of form as soon as possible.

#1737. Luca Williams-Barnett first words revealed after young star signs new Tottenham contract

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Luca Williams-Barnett has hailed his new contract as “a special moment” after committing his future to Tottenham.

The young star has impressed in north London since his breakthrough into the first-team fold under Roberto De Zerbi this term.

The winger notched his first goal for the club at senior level against Ipswich Town after the international break, having made his first senior start at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

He made his Premier League debut off the bench in the win over Crystal Palace, and stepped off the bench in the defeat by Leeds United.

“This is a special moment for me and my family, and one I have worked really hard to reach, but this is only the start,” the 18-year-old said.

“Spurs is a family to me. I've been here for so long – it's a second home, where I trust the people and coaches who have pushed me to become the player I am today.

“The club has trusted and believed in me, now I'm ready to repay that.”

De Zerbi said that the Spurs academy product was a player that he “thought the world of”.

“I'm so happy that he has signed a new contract,” the Italian said.

“He has benefitted from being around the first team every day, growing in stature and consistency, and has deserved his place in the matchday squad over recent weeks.

“Everyone can see how technically gifted Luca is on the pitch but I also love his calmness and decision-making under pressure.

“The best players have confidence on the pitch and humility off it. There is still plenty of room for Luca to improve, and I know he will continue to work hard every day to be the best version of himself.”

#1736. Manchester United star ‘opens door’ to January transfer after Mauricio Pochettino arrival

Ayden Heaven has opened the door to a move away from Manchester United.

That is according to BBC Sport, who claim that the young defender could explore an Old Trafford exit over a lack of playing time.

It is believed that he would prefer a loan move, but he could also leave the club permanently, with Fulham and Barcelona credited with interest.

The 20-year-old has played a bit-part role this term for the Red Devils, often filling in at either centre-back - his preferred position - or left full-back amid an injury crisis in the defensive third.

He was an unused substitute for United’s 4-0 drubbing by Liverpool at Anfield last weekend, as new manager Mauricio Pochettino endured a nightmare start to his tenure in the north west.

United sit 19th in the Premier League table, second from bottom, and mired in the relegation zone after a run of 12 matches with just one victory.

This term, Heaven, who arrived at Old Trafford from Arsenal’s youth setup in February 2025, has played eight times in all competitions.

He replaced Harry Maguire in the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa before the international break, in what proved to be Michael Carrick’s final game in charge before he was sacked.

The young central defender was brought on at half time against Unai Emery’s Villans, with the score at 2-2 after Villa’s quickfire double inside the first four minutes thanks to goals from Alysson and Nicolas Jackson.

Heaven’s most recent start came in the 3-2 win over Roma in the Champions League, partnering Maguire before being substituted for Lisandro Martinez in the 75th minute, with United trailing 2-1.

#1735. GdS: Wins, consistency and goals for Ramos – the next steps Amorim wants Milan to take

Ruben Amorim wants to see more from his AC Milan side, starting this evening against Frosinone, and he believes they are capable.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) report, the aim for today’s match is to ensure the break didn’t disrupt the momentum, ashat happened following the September-October pause when Milan drew away to Sassuolo.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

This time, the opponent will be even tougher (at least based on league position), and Amorim knows it. For this reason, he has demanded the utmost focus from his players and has sought to fire up Gonçalo Ramos, who has only scored twice in the first 11 league matches so far.

The first issue the Portuguese forward needs to address is his finishing. In four matches – against Juventus, Lecce, Bologna, and Inter – he failed to register a single shot, while in two others (against Lazio and Genoa), he didn’t manage to hit the target.

That is simply not enough for a striker who cost €70m, plus bonuses and commissions. However, according to the former Manchester United manager, the fault does not lie with Gonçalo and instead is a team issue.

“Having another forward to assist Ramos and Camarda would certainly be an extra option, but our real problem is that we aren’t reaching the final 30 metres. We are among the worst teams in Serie A when it comes to shots taken and chances created,” he said in his press conference.

“As for Gonçalo, we aren’t putting him in a position to score. Cissé gets into the box with his runs, while Ramos relies on the team’s build-up play. In Genoa, both of our goals came thanks to him. We need to support him better through more possession and quick passing combinations in the final third.

“My goal is to win matches while helping the players perform at their best. We signed Ramos to score goals, but right now, he is helping me more than I am helping him.” A candid admission in defence of the striker he personally pushed to sign.

Compared to the win in Genoa two Sundays ago, Amorim is leaning toward not fielding four attacking players (Moreira, Cisse, Pulisic, and Ramos) from the start.

In yesterday’s training sessions, Cisse was left out of the starting line-up, which featured Musah and Modric in the middle, with Rabiot pushed further forward behind Gonçalo. Pavlovic has been called up and is eager to start, though he is not yet at 100% fitness.

“The choice of formation depends on the opponent and the team’s current state. I don’t believe that scoring more goals or winning more matches is necessarily linked to fielding more attacking players. Frosinone is an attractive side to watch, and speed is their primary weapon,” Amorim added.

“We rank second in Serie A for the number of sprints, and we have the tools to counter both their pace and their one-on-one ability on the flanks. We’ll need to be focused, as they commit more players to the final third than we do and are more clinical than us when winning the ball back.

“As for our season so far? I’m not satisfied with fourth place or all of our performances. We need to play better and achieve more in Europe, but we have grown as a team and in our overall attitude. We must keep moving in this direction.”

He concluded by sharing a Christmas wish regarding the transfer market: “January signings shouldn’t be based on the current league table, but rather on long-term planning. My Christmas wish is for us to win our next seven matches and get our injured players back. That is what I’d like.”

#1734. Arsenal: Mikel Arteta issues David Raya injury update after worrying photo emerges

By Ben Knapton | 23 Nov 2026 14:15

Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya will miss Tuesday's Champions League clash with Borussia Dortmund but appears to have avoided a serious injury, Mikel Arteta has announced.

The Spain international collided with Newcastle United striker Will Osula in the second half of Saturday's 2-2 Premier League draw and had to be replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga.

Raya was in visible pain as an Arsenal physio supported his arm and shoulder, and Arteta admitted at full time that his number one having to come off was "not good news".

The Arsenal boss also revealed that Raya would undergo an MRI scan on Sunday to assess the seriousness of the issue, and on the same day, he was photographed with his arm in a sling in London.

@TouchlineX Raya yesterday in Oxford Circus... https://t.co/6NVmuNDLzZ

However, speaking to reporters in his pre-game press conference, Arteta delivered a reassuring update on Raya, who has seemingly avoided a fracture or dislocation and will not need to go under the knife.

"He’s not fit for tomorrow, but it doesn’t look too serious. We need some more tests tomorrow, but it’s quite encouraging. It seems to be better than expected," Arteta told the media.

"We expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain he had. The first test we have done shows something that is much more encouraging. There is no need for surgery. Tomorrow we will have more tests and we will know [more]."

Arteta did not directly rule Raya out of Sunday's Premier League clash with Manchester City either, potentially handing Arsenal a monumental boost ahead of the visit of Enzo Maresca's side.

The 31-year-old has already kept 10 clean sheets in 16 appearances for the Gunners this season, and he is also believed to have agreed a new long-term contract with Arsenal; his current deal expires in 2028.

Raya has only missed one Arsenal game through injury since originally joining on loan from Brentford in January 2023 - the 5-1 EFL Cup third-round win over Bolton Wanderers in September 2024.

With Raya sidelined, Kepa Arrizabalaga is expected to make just his second Champions League start for Arsenal on Tuesday, after appearing in January's 3-2 victory over Kairat Almaty.

However, Arteta could throw a curveball and select Illan Meslier, whose first and only appearance for the Gunners so far came in their horrendous EFL Cup exit to Fleetwood Town.

The Frenchman has also never played in the Champions League in his career, while Kepa has appeared in the competition 22 times and was Chelsea's starting goalkeeper during their run to the 2022-23 quarter-finals.

As the latter has also held his position as Arteta's number two despite Meslier's arrival, there should be no doubt over Arsenal's starting goalkeeper against Borussia Dortmund.
