#1733. Iraola: Ngumoha must have the time to go step by step

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Andoni Iraola insisted Liverpool talent Rio Ngumoha must be given "the time to go step by step".

Ngumoha continued to shine for the Reds on Sunday as he played a crucial role in their Premier League win over rivals Manchester United.

He (18 years 85 days) became the youngest player to score and assist in a Premier League game for Liverpool since Michael Owen on Boxing Day 1997 (18y 12d v Leeds United).

Ngumoha has also completed more dribbles than any other player through the first four matchdays in this season's Champions League (25). His dribble success rate (73.5%) was also the highest of any player with 10+ completed dribbles (25/34).

However, ahead of Liverpool's Champions League encounter with Club Brugge, Iraola has tempered expectations around the teenager.

"The most difficult part is to keep a very high level consistently," said Iraola.

"You can play a good game then three normal or bad games; especially at a big club like Liverpool, you have to do very well in every game.

"With Rio, I always say we have to give him the time to go step by step. You can't rush it; it wouldn't be fair on him.

"He is in the right mindset and is becoming a better player, adding more things to his game. We know he is good, but we have to leave him sometimes.

"He'll have not so good games, and we have to trust him as he deserves it."

Touching down in Bruges  https://t.co/hpeysX1igJ

This will be the first meeting between Brugge and Liverpool since the 1978 European Cup final, won 1-0 by the Reds at Wembley.

Brugge and Liverpool have faced each other on three previous occasions, with all three of those being in European finals. Both of them were won by the Reds: 4-3 on aggregate in the 1976 UEFA Cup (3-2 at home, 1-1 away) and 1-0 in the 1978 European Cup.

"It's not that they surprised me; I knew they were very good. But honestly I've enjoyed analysing them," Iraola said about Brugge.

"Sometimes you have to watch teams, and it's a little boring, but that's not what happened with Brugge. They are very energetic and have had an incredible run of games, 10 wins and a draw.

"I think we will have to be at a very, very good level, otherwise it is going to be very difficult. They have players who can make the difference, and obviously we also have.

"I expect quite an open game. We are both aggressive, both want to press, and there will be spaces, and hopefully, we can win the one-v-one battles."

#1732. Manchester United dealt blow as Mauricio Pochettino drops hint in confirmed Champions League squad

Manchester United are set to welcome Luke Shaw and Karl Darlow back into the fold for tomorrow night’s Champions League trip to Sporting, but they will be without Matheus Cunha, who was left out of the travelling cohort.

The Brazilian was withdrawn at half time in the 4-0 drubbing from Liverpool over the weekend, replaced by Joshua Zirkzee as the Red Devils trailed 2-0 and were down to ten men after Leny Yoro’s now-overturned red card.

The former Wolves forward is sidelined due to a suspension he picked up from his red card against Roma last time out in Europe.

The return of Shaw, meanwhile, will be appreciated by new boss Mauricio Pochettino, who has the enviable task of shaping a defence that has conceded 34 goals in 18 matches so far this season.

The left-back has missed United’s last eight fixtures with a muscular issue, but the former Southampton defender was pictured in training ahead of Wednesday night’s game.

The 31-year-old is yet to feature in the Champions League this season, rested for the 4-0 win in the opener over Sabah, before injury ruled him out of the next three fixtures.

Backup goalkeeper Darlow has made just one appearance for the Red Devils since joining from rivals Leeds in the summer.

The Welshman was called up for international duty a fortnight ago, playing the first game of the break against Norway before being rested for the second due to a knock.

Darlow was not fit enough to be named on the bench for Sunday’s 4-0 defeat to Liverpool at Anfield, but the 36-year-old was also spotted in training ahead of the Sporting game.

#1731. Maitland-Niles’ last-gasp debut goal salvages Everton’s miserable week

At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

Their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

But here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

"That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP

“Brilliant technique,” said David Moyes, Everton’s manager, who had only introduced Maitland-Niles in the 77th minute after James Garner had succumbed to cramp and could run no more. “We are still getting to know Ainsley but that was a brilliant goal.”

Only those with the coldest hearts would begrudge Everton this point, which was especially hard-earned given they had conceded an 88th-minute header to Benjamin Sesko. But there is no chance a disbelieving Michael Carrick will feel that way.

Benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8

United should, really, have won this game comfortably. Everton were there to be exploited and when Bryan Mbuemo put them ahead early in the second half, they should have powered away into the distance. Everton’s effort was good but they were in danger of losing hope.

Yet, incredibly, United gave Everton two helping hands. They had not been in a position to assist last Tuesday evening, when phone calls from Merseyside to Old Trafford to take Joshua Zirkzee on loan were met with rejection. But the second half display more than made up for that.

“We’re bitterly disappointed,” said Carrick, who was one step removed from having steam puffing from his ears. “All the work that went into putting us in that position at different stages to then come away like that… it’s not a great feeling. It feels like a defeat. It’s a bit of a cliché to say.”

But clichés are true. First United were passive when Tyrique George crashed in a brilliant right-footed drive in the 83rd minute and then, after Sesko profited from Jordan Pickford’s weak hands, they were passive again in allowing Everton to build the move that ended up with Maitland-Niles’ howitzer.

How had it come to this? It was beautiful bedlam, the kind of joy that only football delivers, but for long periods it felt like it was an opportunity for United. There was anticipation that Everton’s fans would create a furnace but there was also the fear it would be dispiritingly quiet.

Had this fixture been at Goodison Park, with its steep stands, tight confines and acoustics that split your ears, United would have been aware of the siege mentality as soon as their bus rolled up outside the stadium but their new sparkling home is rather more hospitable.

This is no criticism of the home crowd – it is anything but. Why should it always fall to them to bail out the failings of those in charge when those in charge, specifically the executives and recruitment department, have given them scant reason to have hope?

The route to victory for United, then, was relatively straightforward: for all Everton’s initial huff and puff, it always appeared that it would be a case of the away team repeating the simple things, retaining their concentration and waiting for a breakthrough.

It could have come as early as the eighth minute. Luke Shaw’s deep cross to the back post picked out Mbuemo, whose cushioned header invited Bruno Fernandes to take aim but the Portuguese’s volley clipped the crossbar with Pickford stranded.

United dominated and Marcus Rashford was central to it all, a scampering presence down the left who gave Merlin Röhl, playing as an auxiliary right-back, all kinds of problems. The only thing missing from his opening 45 minutes was a goal.

When Mbuemo scored so early after the break, it felt as if this was going to be one puncture too many for Everton to withstand and the anticipation was United would get the job done. In all fairness to Moyes, however, he was not in the mood to accept excuses.

His substitutions were all positive, with Jack Grealish changing the mood and Hayden Hackney providing dynamism. But it was the former Middlesbrough man who drove forward to give George, whose loan move from Chelsea was made permanent in June, the opportunity to smash an 83rd-minute bullet past Senne Lammens.

"That was unanswerable!"What a way for Tyrique George to open his account for Everton! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/c0HPRjWUia

“I told the players there would be no excuses and the players all agreed,” Moyes said. “They have hugely bought into it. And, you know, sometimes when you have [fewer] players it means everybody has to be ready. Sometimes when you have a small squad you have to find a way of making it work.”

They did just that. Pickford should have saved the header from Sesko that looked as though it had given United the lift, but Everton, with their manager belligerent and their fans sensing all was not lost, had other ideas. The noise they generated as Maitland-Niles’s goal went in was unique to this stadium.

As Moyes celebrated, shaking his fists and revelling in the positive turn of events, Carrick put his hand across his face and shook his head repeatedly. All the while, Everton’s fans sang I guess that’s why they call it the Blues. United’s head coach certainly had them. Everton, simply, had relief.

2 - For just the second time in the last 50 years, Manchester United have conceded 2+ goals in each of their first three games of a league season, along with 2020-21.Leaky. pic.twitter.com/B2Dk6Ioxkq

It felt like a win. The crowd was with us, we fight to the end and that’s how you get that type of result.

It’s amazing. Everyone wants to start like that and fortunately I did. I put my foot through it and it ended up in the top corner which I’m happy about.

I came here to work hard. It’s a team full of hard workers and I fit right in. I’m going to show I can pull my weight and give as much as everyone else, if not a little bit more.

Even I have a lump in my throat to see him do that after his original move to Everton in August 2021 was stymied by a late change of heart by Mikel Arteta. Don’t normally approve of badge kissers but he has waited such a long time for that and must have thought his chance had gone.

Just time to kick off before the whistle goes. Probably a fair result and that goal from Maitland-Niles was good enough to win a game never mind save it.

Everton 2 Manchester United 2 (Maitland-Niles) Stunning strike! Mazraoui had tackled Dewsbury-Hall in the box after more good work between Grealish and Hackney down the left. But the tackle diverted the ball to Maitland-Niles 25 yards out. And he wrapped his instep around a shot on debut that bent into the top left corner. What a goal!

"That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP

Grealish’s beguiling feet dazzle Mazraoui down the Everton left as he tricks him to reach the byline. He cuts back a pass to Barry who tees up Hackney for a shot that he wafts miles over the bar. Grealish gives him a look as if to say, “Really?”

George finds himself in a near identical spot from which he scored and tries again with a thumping shot that flies into the side-netting via Lammens’ finger tips. He was offside on this occasion, though.

Five minutes of added time for Everton to level again.

Everton 1 Manchester United 2 (Sesko) Sesko wins the ball in the middle and works it out to Bruno Fernandes running down the left. He stops, faces up Maitland-Niles and waits for Shaw to gallop past him before rolling it into the left-back’s stride. Shaw fizzes over a cross that parts Tarkowski’s luxuriant barnet and Sesko, lurking on his shoulder, buries it from eight yards.

Benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8

As Dominic says, below, Manchester United have been asking for this. They have been toothless since Mbeumo’s goal and the only significant threat, Rashford, was taken off for a left-back.

Everton 1 Man Utd 1 (George) A rasping, rising shot that beats Lammens at his near post. He absolutely larruped it after good work by Hackney to put him in space down the right of the box.

"That was unanswerable!"What a way for Tyrique George to open his account for Everton! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/c0HPRjWUia

If you largely try and defend a 1-0 lead and don’t go for that second goal, there’s always the danger of that happening. Superb finish from George to equalise but it’s been so passive from United. Asking for trouble and they’ve got it. Big 7 minutes plus injury time for them now.

Free-kick on the left, parallel with the penalty spot. Hackney bends it in with his right and Branthwaite heads it on target but too close to Lammens who oddly elects to punch.

Mykolenko gives the ball back from the throw-in as Fernandes serves his minute on the sidelines.

Dalot is booked for pulling Grealish’s shirt when the left winger had spun him.

Maitland-Niles receives a warm reception. I had forgotten that he has five England caps.

Bruno Fernandes goes down after kicking Tarkowski’s studs when his foot was raised. The referee does not stop play but books Maguire for complaining when the ball eventually goes out.

Garner almost immediately goes down and starts stretching his calves.

Mykolenko hurls a long throw into the Man Utd box. Dewsbury-Hall meets it with a shot that he catches sweetly but hits a defender. The ball rebounds to Armstrong who scuffs his attempt wide .

George has switched to the right to accommodate Grealish. I wonder if there was ever a possibility of him returning to Villa? Would Unai Emery treasure him?

“He’s back!” the stadium announcer has proclaimed, as Jack Grealish has entered the fray. The move has provided an immediate bounce but let’s see what the former England man can do to change the pattern of the game. Everton believe they have got a £100m player. It’s time to show it.

Grealish’s first contribution sends Mykolenko away on an overlap and Martinez messes up his clearance from the cross, shanking it behind for a corner that they defend soundly.

Manchester United corner on the left after Tielemans’ 25-yard shot was deflected behind. Fernandes plays it along the ground to Shaw in the D. The left-back’s control spoons the ball up with his left so he improvises a right-foot volley with his swinger, dragging it predictably wide.

Rohl is beaten yet again by Rashford and works his way into the book after pulling him back. It’s been hard going for the Everton right back against Rashford but United just haven’t taken advantage of it enough.

Jack Grealish is stripped and ready to come on.

Rashford jinks at pace 35 yards up the inside-left channel, chopping to the left and barrelling between defenders. He takes it too wide to shoot so cutely backheels to Cunha who pulls back his left foot to shoot from six yards but Tarkowski slides his leg through his gait and pokes the ball away. The away fans shout for a penalty but Cunha has no complaints.

Barry diddles Martinez by feinting to the right and then darting left to open a rout to goal. He hammers a shot from about 16 yards that Shaw slides across to block, diverting it to Dewsbury-Hall whose follow-up effort is a tame daisycutter that Lammens easily gathers.

It threatened to be the case that a Manchester United goal would puncture the atmosphere completely and so it has proven. The likelihood here is the away team will score again in the next 10 minutes to completely kill the game. Everton have endured a miserable week and this flat performance is entirely in keeping with the narrative.

Johnson cuts in off the right to run on to Garner’s pass and shoots from 18 yards. Martinez makes himself as big as possible and the shot clips his calf, sending it up before it dips threateningly, whistling over the bar.

Mbeumo heads out Garner’s corner. Dewsbury-Hall crosses it back into the box and Tarkowski tries to head it across into the middle. Manchester United clear their lines.

Shaw slides in to block Dewsbury-Hall’s shot after the attacking midfielder had manipulated an opportunity with a quick interchange with Johnson.

Key for Manchester United, who have taken the lead in a match for the first time this season, not to let up on the tempo with which they started this half.

Everton respond with a menacing cross in from the left, from George, I think, that eludes Johnson as he arrives in the middle a second late.

Everton 0 Manchester United 1 (Mbeumo) United were probing patiently from the kick-off, Mainoo the hub until he helped the ball down the right and Mbeumo drove in from the right touchline, splitting George and Mykolenko until he reached the 18-yard line and wrapped his left instep around a shot that he arrowed into the bottom left corner.

A brilliant run and a fine finish from Bryan Mbeumo! 👏 pic.twitter.com/IM9kVcdPkh

We hadn’t seen that Mbeumo in the first half – so much better, driving inside at pace and with intent. Good decoy run from Fernandes. Top finish from Mbeumo.

Both managers will want to see a lot more urgency from their sides in the second half. Rashford has been United’s most threatening outlet and has the beating of Rohl but Mbeumo and Cunha were poor in those opening 45 minutes and both guilty of turning over the ball cheaply when United were breaking late in the first period. Barry should have hit the target with a header from Rohl’s cross. But it’s been a lacklustre game, low in quality so far.

A drab match that came to life in the last few minutes of the half, creating good a good chance for Thierno Barry and Jarrad Branthwaite thwarting Marcus Rashford and Bruno Fernandes. Everton look wide open on the right side of their defence and Brennan Johnson is starting to make headway against Luke Shaw.

Brilliant sliding tackle from Branthwaite when Rashford, piling down the inside-left channel in full flight. Just as he was about to pull the trigger, Branthwaite launched himself to knock it away and leapt back to his feet to block Fernandes’ stinging follow-up with the his head.

Mykolenko’s long throw from the left raises the Man Utd blood pressure as they try to scramble it clear. The ball pinballs around the six-yard box, comes off Dalot last and straight to Branthwaite who catches it straight and true but clips the shot at Lammens.

There will be three additional minutes. Barry and Johnson link up again to send the rangey striker down the right but again he hits his cross/shot straight at a defender at close quarters. He can’t work an angle but tries to go through a defender.

Rohl and Barry link up in more orthodox fashion with an excellent, dipping cross from the right-back. Barry peels off Maguire and thumps his header wide. That’s the best chance of the game.

Neat one-two between Johnson and Barry sends the latter into the box on the right but his shot/cross is fired straight at Shaw. The crowd shouts ‘Hand ball!’ but it wasn’t and the ref waves play on.

Everton have had no spark at all so far. George goes down when challenged by Mbeumo to give them a free-kick on the left, 35 yards from goal. Garner hits a floaty cross to the right of the box and Barry heads it wide.

It was Johnson who was under scrutiny for a ‘foul’ on Martinez’ but it was just a hand on the back.

Branthwaite is winded when he collides with Pickford in midair defending a back-post cross. Seems to be OK.

Fernandes whips over a cross and Armstrong beats Martínez to head it clear. VAR is looking at Martínez’s claim that he was fouled. Now it’s been cleared.

Yellow card for Johnson for sliding into Cunha’s stride and raising his right boot to leg him up right by the byline on the left, 12 inches outside the area.

Shaw trips Rohl in the Everton penalty area as they fought for the ball from Branthwaite’s block of Rashford’s superb cross from the left. The winger was looking for a near-post runner but Branthwaite read it perfectly, certainly better than Cunha, and telescoped out a leg to intercept.

Given the chaotic end to Everton’s transfer window, the atmosphere was going to go one of two ways: bearpit or flat as a pancake. As of now, it’s very much the latter situation, and not even a first sight of Jack Grealish has enabled the volume to be pumped up. Everton are finding it difficult and special attention will need to be paid to Harrison Armstrong, who has been harshly booked but must now walk a disciplinary tightrope. The young midfielder has played encouragingly once again and is desperate to impress.

Ripples of applause for Grealish who comes off the bench to warm up. Armstrong is urged to shoot when fed by Garner’s curling pass up the inside-right channel. But he dithers and then plays it out to Johnson whose cross is no good.

Best move of the game to date should have ended with Cunha hitting the target. The silkiest bit about it was how Rashford lulled Rohl into a false sense of security with his first touch then tapped the ball past him in the next movement just as Rohl was engaging. Very clever.

Now Shaw reaches the byline down the left and cuts it back for Fernandes. Branthwaite again to the rescue, diligently doing his job and closing down the Man Utd captain. Merlin Röhl is a talented player but he’s no right-back against the well-grooved Rashford and Shaw combo.

Dalot let the Rashford pass through his legs to Cunha, probably deliberately but he might have been better placed to apply the finish himself. Cunha had the time and space to do much better than he did, though.

Cunha blazes a side-foot shot from 18 yards over the bar. It was put on a plate by Rashford’s cut-back from the byline after the winger was sent down the flank by Mbeumo’s clever pass.

Manchester united again open up Everton through the middle when Mainoo slips a pass to Bruno Fernandes who puts his laces through a 25-yard shot that Branthwaite bravely throws himself at and deflects wide and out for a corner.

Tielemans’ eyes widen as space opens up between Armstrong and Garner but he scuffs his 22-yard shot which floats gently down Pickford’s throat.

Shaw cuts out Branthwaite’s long pass to Armstrong who was running down the inside-left channel. Manchester United do not clear their lines convincingly and Everton come back at them, probing away with George and Armstrong.

Dalot is let off a booking inexplicably for pulling George’s arm after being spun by Everton’s left-winger. The crowd is irate at that and seething even more when Armstrong is yellow-carded moments later for wrapping an arm around Fernandes’ neck to stop him running away.

Big shout for a home penalty when Barry goes down, face first in the six-yard box when closed down ny Martínez but it was more of a belly flop than a foul.

Slick attacking move from Manchester United, zipping a dozen passes around Everton and ending with Shaw being slid down the left by Rashford. The left-back crosses from the byline and Mbeumo cushions a header to Bruno Fernandes who flashes a sidewinder volley into the crossbar.

In the grand scheme of things, this might sound the most ridiculous complaint you have read but Manchester United’s kit - really? When they play away at Everton, their kit has always been – and always should be – red shirts, black shorts and black socks. It looks odd with two teams playing in white shorts. This may seem a random observation but there we go... there hasn’t been any action to discuss in the opening four minutes!

Maguire returns to the fray as Everton pass the ball through midfield to Johnson on the right. His cross, aiming for Barry, is cut out by Maguire and cleared to halfway. Back come Everton until Dewsbury-Hall is too rough with Mainoo as the Man Utd midfielder tackled him. Free-kick.

Lammens kicks the ball the full length of the field and Pickford picks it up. Mbeumo momentarily is at right-back with Dalot at centre-half.

Maguire is OK to continue but he will be off the field for the mandatory minute.

Maguire headed the back of Barry’s head and splattered his nose. He should be all right though he might need the cotton wool nostril bungs for a while, like Blackadder, the pencils and ‘wibble’.

Big cheers goes around the stadium when Harrison Armstrong’s name has read out. Everton would likely have sold him had there not been a backlash from fans opposing his sale.

Concern here for Harry Maguire. Looks in distress on the ground, laying very still. Concerned players around.

Leny Yoro is warming up on the touchline.

Looks like he caught the back of Barry’s head as he went to challenge. Sat up nose receiving treatment on a very bloodied nose.

Everton kick off, attacking from right to left. The fans, as usual, are making a racket. Everton work the ball back to Pickford who clips a diagonal up the left. Everton play it towards Barry who collides with Maguire who takes a blow to the head.

The teams emerge from the tunnel, both teams in their home kits with the only twist Manchester United’s switch to white socks.

We’re looking forward to seeing what [Brennan Johnson] does. We know he is very capable [and shown it] in recent seasons. Let’s hope he can bring us goals and assists as he did for Tottenham.

We’ve needed them [the two deadline day signings]. Maitland-Niles is physically fine. I don’t think Jack should be yet. We’ve needed it.

That’s all gone now [deadline day]. It’s all about the football. That’s what people are coming to see and we’ll have to play as well as we have done in our opening two games, get a positive result. Hopefully we can continue to build on it.

Nothing different [expected from the fans today]. They’re always really good for us.

No surprise United remain unchanged from the 5-2 win over Ipswich although Carrick will be looking for his side to score first here and make life a little easier for themselves after going behind to Hull and Ipswich in their opening two games. Brennan Johnson comes in for the departed Iliman Ndiaye, who joined Manchester City for £65m on deadline day. Jack Grealish is on the bench for Everton.

Moyes issued a call to arms to Everton fans in his programme notes after a dismal transfer window that has left him with just 18 outfield players. The Everton manager warning there may be difficult times to come.

“Finally, I must stress the importance of us all pulling together,” Moyes wrote.

“We need to be strong again and there may be occasions when we may have to find a way to get through some difficult moments.

“It is something you have all done in recent seasons. Everyone has pulled together for the good of the football club and we may need to do so again.”

We did a lot of good things [against Ipswich]. No two games are ever the same. We have different challenges today. We have to be ready for that with some slightly different ideas. But the boys did well last week, trained well this week and we’re really looking forward to it.

The next result is always the most important one regardless of what’s happened. Building momentum, building a run, of course it’s important. It’s game-by-game, as you know, but this is as tough as it comes for us, Everton away.

It’s not a major deal, we’ve got the squad and we can cope with it [increase in numbers of fixtures with the return to European football].

Everton  Pickford; Röhl, Tarkowski, Branthwaite, Mykolenko; Armstrong, Garner; Johnson, Dewsbury-Hall, George; Barry. Substitutes Travers, Maitland-Niles, Keane, Grealish, O’Brien, Dibling, Alcaraz, Hackney, Graham.

Man Utd  Lammens; Dalot, Maguire, Martínez, Shaw; Tielemans, Mainoo; Mbeumo, Fernandes, Rashford; Cunha. Substitutes Darlow, Mazraoui, Mount, Zirkzee, Dorgu, Yoro, Santos, Heaven, Sesko.

"Whatever's gone on over the last few days is nothing to do with us as players" James Tarkowski is hoping Everton can get three points against Manchester United 🔵Watch Super Sunday live: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/PMWBO5Oiah

🔴 The Reds are unchanged from last week's win over Ipswich 👊

Mason Mount is fit enough for the bench and takes Shea Lacey’s seat

Brennan Johnson comes in for Iliman Ndiaye, now at Man City. Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Jack Grealish start on the bench.

Today's Toffees to face @ManUtd. COYB! 🔵#EVEMUN pic.twitter.com/8s2UrcwR59

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of Everton vs Manchester United from Hill Dickinson Stadium. The hosts have made a creditable start on the field but four points from their opening two games cannot gloss over the discontent fostered by the owners and executives because of the credibility gap between their talk about recruitment and their paltry achievements.

The fact that their comeback against Bournemouth to earn a draw last week was achieved with Beto, Tim Iroegbunum and Iliman Ndiaye on the field and all three have now been sold with only Jack Grealish returning on loan to compensate tells its own story.

Speak to supporters and it is emblematic of ownership, they fear, who are prioritising Roma and view the Hill Dickinson as a terrific multisport and concert venue with a heritage football club attached. The bullishness of Angus Kinnear, the chief executive, rings hollower with each pronouncement and it is little wonder that the fans are so disenchanted.

David Moyes will not walk away but once again he has been sent into the fray against teams with £250m midfields armed with a spud gun. Having said that, we should not underestimate his capacity to rally the old “dogs of war” spirit even if the crowd is still yearning more for a “school of science” revival.

Manchester United won on their first visit to the Hill Dickinson last season when Benjamin Sesko came off the bench to score the only goal of the game and give Michael Carrick a fifth win in six league games as caretaker manager. They were far more fluid in their forward play during the victory over Ipswich last week but it was against an error-stricken defence and they continued to be as worryingly open at the back as they had been against Hull City in the opening round of fixtures with Luke Shaw and Lisandro Martínez having brain fades.

Shaw is a doubt today, along with Mason Mount, while Amad Diallo, Matthijs de Ligt, Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte have all been ruled out. Only Christian Norgaard is absent for Everton but so thin is their squad, they will cast covetous glances at Man Utd’s bench, not least at Joshua Zirkzee who was the subject of a very late rejected bid on deadline day.

#1730. Can Ethan Nwaneri play against Arsenal for loan club Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League tonight?

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal dropped points from a winning position for the second time in as many games following a 1-1 Champions League draw with Borussia Dortmund at the Emirates Stadium.

Mikel Arteta’s men led at the interval after Viktor Gyokeres scored his first goal on home soil in 206 days with a wonderful 25-yard opener inside 10 minutes.

But just as they did in the Premier League at Newcastle on Saturday, Arsenal were unable to see out the victory, with Maximilian Beier netting for the visitors after half-time.

Jobe Bellingham had a goal ruled out for offside, while Gyokeres could perhaps count himself fortunate not to give away a penalty when a Dortmund corner struck him on the arm.

Gyokeres then wasted a golden opportunity to restore Arsenal’s advantage when he headed wide unmarked from six yards, while the ball cannoned off Serhou Guirassy to twice strike the Dortmund post in the closing stages. Declan Rice hit the woodwork again for Arsenal with five minutes left.

The draw leaves Arsenal fifth in the table, but they could be on the bubble of the top-eight places – which are assured of automatic qualification for the next phase – if results work against them on Wednesday.

#1729. Moretto: Cagliari talent could emerge in Camarda talks with Milan’s interest confirmed

It has been confirmed by a reliable source that Paul Mendy is someone AC Milan are watching closely.

In the past few days, the idea of Francesco Camarda leaving on loan in January has turned from a suggestion into something that seems like a concrete possibility. Given his talent, there has already been interest from a number of clubs.

So, the Milan management must carefully pick the right landing spot for him, and Cagliari have emerged as a suitor. The reason this is something to keep an eye on is because the Rossoneri in turn are keen on one of their forwards, so a mutually beneficial arrangement could arise.

According to Matteo Moretto’s latest update on Fabrizio Romano’s YouTube channel, an explorative contact took place a couple of weeks ago between Camarda’s entourage and Cagliari. They are an option for him, but there are also other options for the Italian in Italy and abroad as well.

Meanwhile, the journalist also confirmed that Cagliari forward Paul Mendy appeals to Milan just like he appeals to several other clubs. Milan are interested, but there is nothing advanced to talk about at the moment.

Mendy is 19 years of age and he burst onto the scene last season, scoring his first two Serie A goals for the Sardinian side. He has one goal and two assists in the league so far this season.

#1728. Man United predicted lineup vs. Sporting Lisbon: De Ligt, Zirkzee decisions, Cunha blow

By Oliver Thomas | 23 Nov 2026 14:45, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 15:11

Mauricio Pochettino could be without as many as seven Manchester United players for Wednesday’s Champions League clash with Sporting Lisbon at the Estadio Jose Alvalade.

Former Sporting midfielder Manuel Ugarte (knee), Carlos Baleba (hamstring) and Benjamin Sesko (calf) all remain sidelined with injuries, while Luke Shaw (muscle), Marcus Rashford (hip) and Karl Darlow (knee) are all doubtful and will need assessing ahead of kickoff.

Matheus Cunha scored two late goals in Man United’s 3-2 comeback victory over Roma on matchday four, but he was then sent off for two bookable offences and will now serve a one-match suspension on Wednesday.

Leny Yoro, meanwhile, is available to return to the UCL squad after serving his own one-game ban following a red card against Atletico Madrid last month – he also received a straight red card in Man United’s heavy 4-0 Premier League defeat to Liverpool on Sunday, but will instead serve a domestic ban for that dismissal.

Yoro could therefore continue as a centre-back against Sporting, with Pochettino to weigh up whether to stick with a back three/five system with wing-backs or revert to a four-man defence.

Matthijs de Ligt was handed his first PL start in 357 games by Pochettino after recovering from a long-term injury, but the Dutchman endured a difficult return to the Red Devils side and may be pulled out of the starting lineup in midweek.

Harry Maguire would be the most likely name to replace De Ligt and could start as one of three central defenders next to Yoro and Lisandro Martinez, with Diogo Dalot and Patrick Dorgu operating as wing-backs.

Noussair Mazraoui is an alternative who could start as a right or left-sided full-back in a back four, or as a wing-back, with Dalot potentially operating on the opposite side, allowing Dorgu to push further forward and play in an attacking role.

Kobbie Mainoo, Youri Tielemans and captain Bruno Fernandes are expected to continue in their central midfield roles, the latter is set to face his former club for the first time since leaving to join Man United in January 2020.

Bryan Mbeumo could retain his starting spot as a centre-forward, but Pochettino may be tempted to hand Joshua Zirkzee a rare start up front, with Mbeumo moving over to the right side of attack. However, Amad Diallo could instead play on the right which would likely keep Mbeumo through the middle.

Manchester United possible starting lineup:

Lammens; Yoro, Maguire, Martinez; Dalot, Mainoo, Tielemans, Dorgu; Mbeumo, Fernandes; Zirkzee

#1727. Spurs youngster Williams-Barnett signs new contract

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Tottenham youngster Luca Williams-Barnett has signed a new contract with the club.

The 18-year-old's previous deal was set to expire in June 2028, but he has now reportedly extended his stay at the club by five years.

Williams-Barnett made his Premier League debut for Spurs last month in their win over Crystal Palace, while also featuring off the bench against Leeds United before starting against Ipswich Town.

Against Ipswich on Saturday, Williams-Barnett (18 years 51 days) became the second-youngest player ever to both score and assist in a Premier League game, older only than Michael Owen in 1997 (17y 364d).

He was also the youngest player to score for Spurs in the Premier League since Gareth Bale against Fulham in September 2007 (18y 47d), and the fourth-youngest player to score on his first Premier League start behind Daniel Jebbison in May 2021 (17y 276d), Danny Cadamarteri in September 1997 (17y 343d), and Mark Cullen in May 2010 (18y 12d).

Williams-Barnett, who joined Spurs at the age of 10, has made five senior appearances in total, and could play an important role under Roberto De Zerbi.

"This is a special moment for me and my family, and one I have worked really hard to reach. But this is only the start," the teenager told the Spurs website.

We are delighted to announce that Luca Williams-Barnett has signed a new contract with the Club. Congrats, Luca  https://t.co/Ih7y5K9Grh https://t.co/UJq6mCNBDR

— Tottenham Hotspur (@SpursOfficial) November 24, 2026

"Spurs is a family to me. I've been here for so long – it's a second home, where I trust the people and coaches who have pushed me to become the player I am today.

"The club has trusted and believed in me; now I'm ready to repay that."

De Zerbi added: "Luca is a player I think the world of, and I'm so happy that he has signed a new contract.

"He has benefited from being around the first team every day, growing in stature and consistency, and has deserved his place in the matchday squad over recent weeks.

"Everyone can see how technically gifted Luca is on the pitch, but I also love his calmness and decision-making under pressure.

"The best players have confidence on the pitch and humility off it. There is still plenty of room for Luca to improve, and I know he will continue to work hard every day to be the best version of himself."

#1726. How Arsenal will change tactics to suit Kepa in goalkeeper’s last chance to impress

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Any and all updates on David Raya were welcome if you were an Arsenal fan.

There were the attempts to lip read what head physio Simon Murphy said as he walked off the St James’ Park pitch with Raya.

Then the sighting of Raya the following day in Oxford Circus with his arm in a sling. And the report that he had been able to drive himself home after the club returned to London from Newcastle.

The sense of panic was understandable. Raya is Arsenal’s most irreplaceable player, pivotal to the team not just because of his shot-stopping, but the way he commands his area and how central he is to the build-up in possession as well.

It was good news, then, that he has avoided a serious injury. Raya has not yet been ruled out of facing Manchester City this weekend.

Even with the outlook more positive than it might have been, Arsenal must still find a way to cope without the Spaniard for at least tonight’s match against Borussia Dortmund.

This will be a big night for Kepa Arrizabalaga. He started against Kairat Almaty last season, but that dead rubber aside has not played in the Champions League since making four appearances for Real Madrid in the competition in 2023.

This is a chance to prove he still belongs at this level. Kepa will surely still have an eye on becoming a first-choice goalkeeper again at a top club elsewhere in the seasons ahead. However, that kind of evidence has been in short supply since he arrived at Arsenal.

Mikel Arteta put his faith in Kepa last season in the Carabao Cup final and it was not repaid. Kepa was booked for hauling down Jeremy Doku after misjudging a bouncing ball, before gifting City the lead when spilling a cross.

His distribution, too, was poor. Throughout the match, Arsenal’s build-up was almost entirely nullified by City and that started with the goalkeeper.

A key facet of Arsenal’s build-up is Raya’s ability to not just go short, but to ping flat, long passes up the pitch to play over the press when required.

It is easy to forget just how highly rated Kepa once was, he remains the most expensive goalkeeper signing of all time

Discover a hidden island paradise in the Indian Ocean

“David Raya can play six, I swear,” Noni Madueke said in a recent interview.

Kepa cannot play those same passes with the same trajectory or accuracy. Nor is he as convincing in inspiring the same confidence when going short under pressure.

Asked on Monday whether Arsenal would have to change how they play without Raya, Arteta said: “We adapt to players’ qualities, and they all have different ones.

“There are certain things that, in our game or in the way that we understand the game and we want to play the game, everybody has to be 100% committed to, but then we make adjustments in relation to the qualities of the players.”

One of those adjustments will have to be how Arsenal build up. Illan Meslier would be more comfortable in that respect, with the ball at his feet, but he is liable to make big mistakes and can be exposed when the ball is crossed on top of him.

There has never been any real consideration from Arteta or his coaching staff that it would be Meslier getting the nod over Kepa to stand in for Raya.

When he signed in the summer, Meslier was aware of the pecking order. He arrived primarily to allow Tommy Setford to go out on loan, rather than to replace Kepa as No2.

Meslier started in the Carabao Cup defeat to Fleetwood, even with Kepa fit and in the squad. However, that was due to a desire to reward Meslier for his consistency in training and impact on the squad, not a rejigging of the pecking order.

It is easy to forget just how highly rated Kepa once was. He remains the most expensive goalkeeper signing of all time, joining Chelsea for £72million in 2018.

That price tag has followed him around ever since. So too Carabao Cup finals, both last season’s horror show and the 2019 edition when he refused to be substituted.

The temptation is to say a quiet night, one in which he is not noticed against Dortmund, would be ideal for Kepa, but Raya does not have many of those.

Even when he is not required to pull off saves, he is still making line-breaking passes or pushing up close to the halfway line to snuff out attacks.

Kepa failed on all those counts in the Carabao Cup final last season. Another poor performance this time and it is hard to see how he can retain Arteta’s trust.

In his biggest test since that Wembley occasion, Arsenal need Kepa to minimise the disruption of Raya’s absence.

#1725. Rangers vs Aberdeen - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 23 Nov 2026 15:29, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 15:34

Rangers play host to Aberdeen on Tuesday night looking to move to within one point of leaders Celtic in the Scottish Premiership table.

Meanwhile, Aberdeen make the trip to Ibrox knowing that they could move into the top six with a surprise win over the Glasgow giants.

Although missing out on European football came as a major blow to Rangers at the time, it has enabled Derek McInnes's side to build up a head of steam on the domestic front.

Rangers have put together a 13-match unbeaten streak since that exit to Jablonec in the Conference League playoff round, recording 11 wins and two draws.

While being held to a 2-2 draw at Hearts before the November international break frustrated McInnes, Rangers have responded with a victory over Aberdeen in the League Cup and successive top-flight triumphs.

A 2-0 success at St Mirren was followed by an hard-earned 2-1 win at Motherwell on Saturday, Rangers sealing the three points through an 88th-minute own goal.

Eight of Rangers' 13 league matches have been played away from Ibrox, giving them a chance to make the most of competing on home territory, with seven goals being scored in their last two such games in the Scottish Premiership.

Over the international break, Liechtenstein legend Mario Frick was named as the new Aberdeen head coach.

The surprise development was followed by Frick delivering a 4-2 victory at Kilmarnock in his first game in charge.

A much-needed win has led to the Dons moving into eighth spot, albeit still just three points above the relegation zone.

With Aberdeen having lost five of the six matches preceding his arrival, Frick will not be getting carried away with three points versus bottom-of-the-table opposition.

Nevertheless, Aberdeen have now accumulated seven points from their most recent four away games in the Scottish Premiership, something which cannot be ignored by their hosts.

If McInnes makes any changes to his Rangers XI, Findlay Curtis and Kevin Kelsy are favourites to be introduced in the final third.

While Cameron Devlin is making progress in his recovery from injury, this game is expected to come too soon for the midfielder. The same applies to Lawrence Shankland, who has recently returned to light training after a significant hamstring injury.

Ryan Naderi has contributed either a goal or assist in eight of his last nine Scottish Premiership appearances.

Afeez Aremu, Findlay Marshall and Ayoub Mouloua are all options to return for Aberdeen after they made an impact from the substitutes' bench at Kilmarnock.

Connor Ronan remains an injury doubt after missing that fixture, while this match comes too soon for defender Mats Knoester. Chris Cadden is pushing for a return to the squad after a hamstring issue.

Pandur; Sterling, Makhanya, Fernandez, Rommens; Neil, Raskin; Bouanani, Naderi, Findlay; Kelsy

Muller; Devlin, Milne, Molloy, Guinness-Walker; Lyons, Aremu, Briedl; Marshall; Mouloua, Nisbet

With Aberdeen having made a positive start to life under Frick, they will back themselves to earn a result at Ibrox. However, given the chance to move within a point of Celtic, we feel that Rangers will do just enough to secure three points in a competitive fixture.

#1724. Arsenal XI vs Borussia Dortmund: Starting lineup, confirmed team news and injury latest for Champions League

Arsenal take on Borussia Dortmund this evening as they return to action in the Champions League. It’s the Premier League champions against the Bundesliga leaders tonight, and Mikel Arteta’s side will be hoping to produce a statement performance to continue their unbeaten run on the continent.

#1723. MN: Cardinale working on second renewal as Amorim picks Milan’s two ‘irreplaceables’

Ruben Amorim is not a coach who makes a habit of singling out individuals, but he made an exception in Saturday’s press conference.

As MilanNews recall, on the eve of the game against Frosinone, Amorim bluntly admitted that Christian Pulisic and Adrien Rabiot are the ‘irreplaceable’ players in the current squad. Their characteristics and their quality make them unique, in the eyes of the coach and many fans.

When the American and the Frenchman don’t play, the team’s fluidity and effectiveness suffer significantly. There is a stark contract between Milan when Rabiot and Pulisic play versus when both do not feature.

Amorim’s words were clear in his pre-match presser: “Every player appreciates having the club’s trust. And Pulisic’s new contract has helped. When he wasn’t playing, I told you he was still important for Milan, and we can’t forget about the injured players.

“Pulisic is the only player we can’t replace today: the way he moves between the lines, we don’t have another Pulisic. In the last few European matches, we missed him; we had to manage him. If he’s not on the pitch, given his characteristics, you feel it.

“And you understand how important he is. He doesn’t talk much, but he speaks a lot on the pitch with his play. He always wants the ball. He and Rabiot always lift the team up. I don’t like to talk about individuals, but I have to.

“I think everyone can understand that. So Pulisic is our present, he will be our future, and I think he has the potential to do even more.”

It’s worth noting that the coach emphasised the importance of Pulisic’s contract renewal too. This is also why the club are doing everything possible to reach an agreement for Rabiot.

Cardinale called him a top player and candidly admitted that he adores him, also emphasising how he respects his family. These statements are not coincidental, given that it is his mother who represents the midfielder.

Speaking of which, discussions with Véronique Rabiot are progressing positively. A meeting took place before the derby, which ended with a 3-1 win with a goal for the former Juventus and Marseille midfielder.

The player is happy with the Rossoneri and wants to stay: a definitive agreement on the financial terms needs to be reached. Milan are also willing to adjust the player’s salary in order to secure him for a few more years at Milanello.

#1721. Inter Milan vs Stuttgart - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 23 Nov 2026 15:39, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 13:43

Separated by one point midway through the league phase, Inter Milan and Stuttgart will meet for a Champions League clash at San Siro on Wednesday evening.

After contrasting results last time out, Inter trail behind their German visitors, with both sides vying for entry to the knockout round playoffs.

Having exited at the first knockout stage last season - losing both playoff legs to Bodo/Glimt - Inter started this term's Champions League campaign slowly, taking nothing from their first two fixtures.

The Scudetto holders subsequently bounced back, though, posting consecutive wins without conceding a goal, against Shakhtar Donetsk and Feyenoord.

Shortly before the international break, Inter travelled to De Kuip and left with maximum points, thanks to goals from Yann Bisseck, Francesco Pio Esposito and Piotr Zielinski.

Such a start sums up their mixed fortunes since being humbled by Paris Saint-Germain in the 2025 final: Cristian Chivu's Champions League record as head coach reads seven wins and seven defeats.

Compared to life under his predecessor Simone Inzaghi, the Nerazzurri have been much less solid at the back, and they shipped yet more goals in a spectacular Serie A contest on Sunday night.

Despite Esposito's hat-trick, Inter ultimately had to settle for a 4-4 draw against local rivals Atalanta, and that left them three points behind surprise league leaders Lazio.

In stark contrast to their Italian counterparts, Stuttgart kicked off the league phase with back-to-back victories, scoring three goals against both Slovan Bratislava and Viking.

Then, they held Atletico Madrid to a 1-1 home draw, before visiting Istanbul to face Turkish champions Galatasaray on matchday four.

Already trailing by two goals inside 15 minutes, the German club never really recovered, suffering their first loss and slipping down to 14th place in the Champions League standings.

Despite holding on to highly-rated coach Sebastian Hoeness, Die Roten have struggled in the Bundesliga this season, losing half of their first 10 games.

While Inter were sharing eight goals in Bergamo, Stuttgart played out a 0-0 draw with Schalke last weekend, leaving them eighth in the table and eight points behind the top four.

Still, the Swabian side have recently improved a once porous defence, posting three clean sheets from four domestic matches before heading to Milan.

Although Inter threw away two points against Atalanta, they were able to welcome back their inspirational captain, as Lautaro Martinez made his return from injury with a late cameo.

Having conceded a stoppage-time penalty against his former club, Alessandro Bastoni will hope to fare better on Wednesday, when he returns from a Champions League suspension.

Benjamin Pavard made 88 appearances for Stuttgart between 2016 and 2019, and the Frenchman may join Bastoni in a three-man defence.

The hosts will be missing key midfielder and set-piece specialist Hakan Calhanoglu due to a thigh injury, while Ange Bonny is also ruled out.

Martinez must vie with Marcus Thuram and Manchester United target Esposito to feature up front, but there is no doubt about Stuttgart's star striker.

Ermedin Demirovic has already netted a club-record four goals in this season's Champions League campaign, added to five in the Bundesliga.

By contrast, Deniz Undav has yet to score in the German top flight, but he is still set to support Demirovic at San Siro.

Though Hoeness has most of his squad available, Luca Jaquez (rib), Leo Sauer (muscular) and Angelo Stiller (groin) are currently injured.

J. Martinez; Pavard, Akanji, Bastoni; Spence, Barella, Zielinski, Sucic, Dimarco; Esposito, L. Martinez

Bredlow; Hendriks, Chabot, Mittelstadt; Leweling, Karazor, Promel, Fuhrich; Undav, El Khannouss; Demirovic

It's either hit or miss for Inter, who have drawn none of their last 16 Champions League matches, and the Serie A champions will extend that trend with a home win.

Half of their goals in the league phase have arrived inside the final 15 minutes, so Stuttgart may be caught out in the closing stages.

#1720. Prediction: Crystal Palace vs Real Sociedad

Thomas Frank takes charge of his first home match as Crystal Palace manager on Thursday night when the Eagles welcome Real Sociedad to Selhurst Park in the Europa League.

The two sides are level on five points after four league-phase matches, having each recorded one win, two draws and one defeat. With Crystal Palace sitting 21st and Real Sociedad 20th in the standings, both clubs know a victory could provide a significant boost to their hopes of reaching the knockout rounds.

Crystal Palace are still searching for an upturn in fortunes after a difficult season that has left them bottom of the Premier League table.

Thomas Frank’s first game in charge ended in a 3-2 defeat away to Coventry City, extending Palace’s losing streak in the league to five matches. Although Frank praised the effort and passion shown by his players, the Eagles have now suffered eight defeats from their opening 11 league fixtures, with meagre seven points on the board.

Defensive problems have been a recurring theme throughout the campaign. Only Manchester United have conceded more goals across Europe’s top five leagues this season, with Palace shipping 33 goals in all competitions. They have also conceded at least twice in 11 of their 17 matches.

European football has at least offered some encouragement. The reigning Conference League champions are unbeaten in their last eight major European home matches, winning five and drawing three. Frank also boasts a strong home record in Europe from his previous spells with Tottenham Hotspur and Brondby, suffering just one defeat in nine such games.

However, Palace have failed to win any of their last three Europa League matches. Defeats to Lyon and draws against Besiktas and Hoffenheim have left them outside the top places, although Daichi Kamada’s dramatic 91st-minute equaliser against Hoffenheim earned a valuable point three weeks ago.

With only two points separating them from the top eight, Thursday’s match could prove crucial in the race for automatic qualification to the last 16.

Crystal Palace remain without Chadi Riad, Ismaila Sarr and Takehiro Tomiyasu through injury, while Oscar Mingueza is a doubt after picking up a knock at the weekend.

Yeremy Pino and Jean-Philippe Mateta are suspended domestically and should therefore start in Europe, but midfielder Adam Wharton is unavailable after accumulating yellow cards in the competition.

Frank switched to a four-man defence against Coventry and could keep that system in place. Jaydee Canvot, Honest Ahanor and Axel Disasi are competing for a place alongside Chris Richards in central defence, while Ben Chilwell could replace Tyrick Mitchell at left-back.

Real Sociedad have experienced a mixed return to European football after missing out on continental competition last season.

The Spanish side started their Europa League campaign with a 2-1 home defeat against Bournemouth before drawing with Union SG and Lyon. Their standout result came on matchday three when they thrashed Lillestrom 6-0 away from home.

Domestically, Pellegrino Matarazzo’s side have also struggled for consistency. Over their last 10 matches in all competitions, they have recorded five wins, two draws and three defeats. Most recently, La Real suffered a 3-2 loss away to Racing Santander in La Liga.

Despite that setback, Real Sociedad remain fifth in La Liga and are still chasing a top-four place, although they currently sit five points adrift. Important matches against Sevilla, Real Madrid and Villarreal are looming, but their immediate focus is on strengthening their Europa League position.

The visitors are aiming to reach the Europa League knockout rounds for the sixth time in six appearances since the competition was rebranded in 2009-10. Their record against English opposition, however, is not encouraging. Real Sociedad have won only one of their last 11 meetings with English clubs, a 1-0 victory away to Manchester United in the 2022-23 group stage. Matarazzo himself has managed only two wins from eight Europa League matches as a coach.

Alvaro Odriozola continues to recover from a long-term knee injury, while Ander Barrenetxea recently underwent surgery on a hamstring problem and faces an extended spell on the sidelines.

Jon Martin could come into central defence alongside Igor Zubeldia, replacing Chelsea loanee Mamadou Sarr. Hector Fort and Sergio Gomez are expected to feature as full-backs.

Captain Mikel Oyarzabal has yet to score in the Europa League this season, but he is expected to retain his place in attack ahead of Orri Oskarsson. He could be supported by Goncalo Guedes, Luka Sucic and Takefusa Kubo.

Both teams enter the contest looking to rebound from disappointing domestic defeats, and neither side can realistically afford another setback in Europe.

Crystal Palace’s defensive issues continue to undermine their performances, but their strong home record in continental competition offers encouragement. Real Sociedad have shown flashes of quality throughout the league phase, yet have struggled for consistency and historically have not enjoyed much success against English opponents.

With both teams carrying attacking threats and defensive vulnerabilities, this has the makings of an entertaining encounter that could produce goals at both ends.

84 mins: Just over five minutes to play of regulation time. Can either side find a winner?

81 mins: Close! Another sumptuous ball from Odegaard low and into the POMO, and somehow it stays out! Hincapie keeps it alive, it comes off Guirassy, off the upright twice and away!

80 mins: Free kick, Arsenal. Handball by Sabitzer. Another chance for the hosts to hoist one into the box towards their big lads.

78 mins: Arteta skipping around that touchline now, extremely animated. Fair to say Gyokeres missing a free header from a few yards out hasn’t helped his manager’s mood.

77 mins: What a miss! A delicious delivery from Odegaard, begging to be put in by Gyokeres, who nods wide from close range!
